note: A solid yellow light means the signal is about to turn red. You must stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are too close to stop safely when it turns yellow, continue through carefully rather than braking hard in the intersection.

question: When riding in a vehicle, what is true about small children?
options: a:May be safely held by a strong adult.,b:Must be properly secured in an appropriate child restraint for their size and age.,c:Will be safe if standing on the floor in the back of the vehicle.
note: Small children must always be secured in a properly installed child safety seat or booster seat that is appropriate for their age, height, and weight. Holding a child in your arms or allowing them to stand in the vehicle is extremely dangerous and illegal in all states.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must not drive faster than which speed?
options: a:A speed that is reasonable and prudent for conditions, not exceeding posted limits.,b:The maximum speed limit only.,c:A speed that is safe for existing conditions only.
note: You must never drive faster than is safe for current conditions, and you may not exceed the posted speed limit. Even if the limit is higher, you must slow down for rain, fog, heavy traffic, or poor visibility so your speed is both legal and safe.

question: A diamond-shaped warning sign tells drivers:
options: a:Alerts drivers to public recreation areas.,b:Warns of existing or possible hazards.,c:Alerts drivers to school zones.
note: Diamond-shaped signs are general warning signs. They alert you to existing or possible hazards or changes in road conditions ahead so you can slow down, look carefully, and be prepared to react.

question: Must a motorist making a left turn yield to an oncoming bicyclist?
options: a:True — yield to oncoming bicycles like any other vehicle.,b:False
note: Bicycles are vehicles and have the same right-of-way as cars. When turning left, you must yield to oncoming traffic, including bicyclists, and only turn when it is safe and will not force them to slow or stop suddenly.

question: The color orange on signs usually indicates:
options: a:School zone signs.,b:Work zone signs.,c:Regulatory signs.
note: Orange signs are used for construction and maintenance work zones. They warn you of workers, equipment, lane shifts, or other temporary conditions so you can slow down and drive with extra caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Are you allowed to exceed the posted speed limit to complete a pass on roads with speed limits under 55 mph?
options: a:False — you may not exceed the posted speed limit to pass.,b:True — you may go over the limit briefly to complete a pass.
note: You must never exceed the posted speed limit to pass another vehicle. If you cannot safely complete a pass without speeding, you must wait for a longer clear distance or not pass at all.

question: After an upsetting incident at work, what is the safest action before driving home?
options: a:Play loud music to distract yourself.,b:Drive fast to release emotions.,c:Take a few minutes to calm down before driving.,d:Call a friend while driving to vent.
note: Strong emotions like anger or frustration can distract you from the road, slow your reactions, and lead to risky decisions. The safest choice is to wait until you have calmed down before driving so you can focus fully on traffic and road conditions.

question: Which effects are commonly caused by alcohol?
options: a:Loss of concentration.,b:Poor coordination.,c:Slower judgment.,d:All of the above.
note: Alcohol affects the brain and nervous system, reducing concentration, slowing judgment and reaction time, and harming coordination. Because it impairs several skills at once, all of the listed effects can occur, which greatly increases the risk of a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left onto a one-way street, where should you complete the turn?
options: a:The right lane.,b:The lane closest to your previous lane.,c:Either lane.
note: When turning left onto a one‑way street, you should enter the lane that is nearest to the lane you turned from. This keeps traffic organized, prevents sudden lane changes in the intersection, and reduces the chance of conflicts with other vehicles.

question: You must come to a stop at an intersection when you see which signal?
options: a:Steady yellow light.,b:Yellow arrow.,c:Flashing red light.
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. After stopping, proceed only when the intersection is clear and it is safe to go.

question: Which of the following does NOT help promote safe night driving?
options: a:Keep your windshield clean.,b:Carry a flashlight in your vehicle.,c:Install heavy window tinting that reduces nighttime visibility.,d:Use low-beam headlights in poor visibility.
note: Safe night driving depends on maximizing your ability to see and be seen. Clean windows and proper use of low‑beam headlights help visibility, and a flashlight can be useful if you must stop. Very dark window tinting that reduces your ability to see at night makes driving more dangerous, not safer.

question: If you are stopped by a police officer, what should you do while waiting for the officer to approach?
options: a:Unbuckle your seat belt and lower your window,b:Get your paperwork ready before the officer reaches your car,c:Stay in your vehicle with your hands visible on the steering wheel and wait for the officer to approach,d:Exit your vehicle and walk to the officer
note: If stopped by police, stay in the vehicle unless directed otherwise, keep your hands clearly visible on the steering wheel, and have passengers keep their hands visible as well. Wait calmly for the officer to approach and ask for your documents before reaching for anything.

question: How can you avoid alcohol-related crashes?
options: a:Decide before you start drinking that you will not drive.,b:Simply say no if offered a drink, then drive.,c:Call a taxi only after you've been drinking heavily.
note: The safest way to avoid alcohol‑related crashes is to decide before you start drinking that you will not drive. Plan a sober driver, use transit or a rideshare, or avoid drinking if you must drive. Decisions made after drinking are unreliable because your judgment is already impaired.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing, what precautions should you take?
options: a:Slow down, look for a train, and be ready to stop.,b:Only slow if you see flashing lights.,c:Always change gears before crossing tracks.
note: When approaching a railroad crossing, slow down and be prepared to stop. Look and listen carefully for trains in both directions. If lights are flashing or gates are down, you must stop between 15 and 50 feet from the tracks and never drive around lowered gates.

question: At an intersection with a flashing red light, what must you do?
options: a:Come to a full stop and proceed when safe.,b:Slow and drive through if clear.,c:Stop only if a police officer is present.
note: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, yield to any traffic or pedestrians in or close to the intersection, and then proceed only when it is safe and your path is clear.

question: Which is a common sign of a drunk driver?
options: a:Weaving between lanes.,b:Driving more slowly than traffic.,c:Always making quick and sudden stops.
note: Weaving between lanes is a classic sign of an impaired driver because alcohol affects coordination and lane control. Other signs can include inconsistent speeds, sudden braking, and wide turns, but noticeable weaving is one of the most common and dangerous behaviors.

question: Is liability insurance required for every motor vehicle in Minnesota?
options: a:True — every motor vehicle must be covered by liability insurance.,b:False — insurance is optional.,c:Only required for commercial vehicles.,d:Only required for vehicles older than 10 years.
note: Minnesota law requires every motor vehicle to carry liability insurance, and drivers must have proof of insurance available when operating the vehicle. Liability insurance helps pay for injuries or damage you cause to others in a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a street from a driveway, what must you do?
options: a:Must drive slowly to allow approaching vehicles and pedestrians time to get out of your way.,b:Must stop and proceed only when there are no pedestrians or vehicles approaching.,c:Must honk your horn so approaching vehicles and pedestrians know to give you room.
note: When entering a street from a driveway or alley, you must stop before the sidewalk or curb line and yield to pedestrians and all approaching traffic. Only proceed when it is safe and you will not force others to slow or change lanes suddenly.

question: A flashing red traffic signal should be treated the same as which sign?
options: a:A slow sign.,b:A yield sign.,c:A stop sign.,d:A no-passing sign.
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. After stopping, yield to any traffic or pedestrians in or close to the intersection, then proceed only when it is safe.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, which way should you turn the steering wheel?
options: a:In the direction you want the vehicle to go.,b:In the opposite direction of the skid.,c:To keep the front wheels straight.
note: In a skid, you should steer in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go, which is usually the same direction the rear of the vehicle is skidding. This helps you regain control; then gently straighten the wheel as the vehicle begins to respond.

question: Which of these can impair a person's ability to drive safely?
options: a:Alcohol.,b:Any medication, including some over-the-counter drugs.,c:A lack of sleep.,d:All of the above.
note: Driving can be impaired by alcohol, many prescription and over‑the‑counter medications, illegal drugs, and fatigue. Any of these can slow your reaction time, affect judgment, and reduce coordination, making it unsafe to drive. Always read medication warnings and avoid driving if you feel drowsy or impaired.

question: If a green arrow changes to a solid green light, what must you do when turning?
options: a:You may still turn but must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,b:You may not turn and must proceed straight.,c:You have exclusive right-of-way to turn.,d:You must stop and wait for a green arrow.
note: When a protected green arrow ends and you get a solid green light, your turn becomes an unprotected turn. You may still turn in that direction, but you must first yield to oncoming traffic, bicyclists, and pedestrians in the crosswalk. Make the turn only when there is a safe gap.

question: What is the correct use of a freeway exit ramp regarding braking?
options: a:Slow down before entering the exit ramp.,b:Maintain speed until you are on the exit ramp, then slow down.,c:Keep constant speed once on the exit ramp.,d:Stop at the start of the exit ramp and then coast down.
note: On freeways, you should not slow down on the main travel lanes before your exit, because that can surprise drivers behind you and cause rear‑end collisions. Signal, move into the exit lane, and then reduce speed in the deceleration lane or on the exit ramp as indicated by signs and conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If someone drives much slower than the speed limit and causes a backup, what is required?
options: a:They should pull off the road and let following cars pass when safe.,b:They always have the right of way.,c:They are the safest drivers.
note: Driving much slower than the flow of traffic can be just as dangerous as speeding because it can cause sudden braking and passing. If you are traveling well below the speed limit and causing a line of vehicles behind you, you should safely pull off the road or into a turnout area when possible and let other vehicles pass.

question: Are cell phones a serious source of driver distraction?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Cell phones are a major source of distraction because they take your eyes off the road, your hands off the wheel, and your mind off driving. Even hands‑free conversations reduce your attention. Use a phone only when absolutely necessary and legal, such as to report an emergency, and never text while driving.

question: What is the most important thing to remember about speed management when driving through curves?
options: a:Accelerate gently before entering the curve.,b:Slow down before you enter the curve.,c:Drive at the posted speed and then brake at the sharpest part.,d:Increase speed while in the curve to maintain momentum.
note: Before entering a curve, slow to a safe speed so you can steer smoothly and stay in your lane. In a curve, inertia tends to push your vehicle outward; entering too fast makes it harder to control the vehicle and increases the risk of skidding or crossing the center line. Adjust speed before the curve, then maintain a steady speed through it.

question: After stopping for a school bus unloading children, what should you do before proceeding?
options: a:Watch carefully for children walking along the roadside and proceed only when clear.,b:Proceed once children wave to you.,c:Accelerate quickly to clear the bus area.
note: After stopping for a school bus with its red lights flashing and stop arm extended, you must remain stopped until the signals are turned off. When the bus’s lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn, proceed slowly and be prepared to stop again. Children may cross unexpectedly or walk along the roadside, so scan carefully in all directions and move forward only when the area is clearly safe.

question: Which factors influence the effects of alcohol on a person?
options: a:Amount of food in the stomach, body weight, and time between drinks.,b:Only how much you enjoy the beverage.,c:Whether you are driving before drinking.
note: The effect of alcohol depends on several physical and timing factors, not on how much you like the drink. Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) is influenced by how much alcohol you consume, how quickly you drink it, your body weight, and whether there is food in your stomach, which can slow absorption. Even with food, alcohol still impairs driving, so you should never rely on food to make drinking and driving safe.

question: When an emergency vehicle approaches with lights and siren, you must pull over and allow it to pass:
options: a:Only if it is following you.,b:Only if it is approaching you from the opposite direction.,c:Regardless of its direction, you must pull to the right edge of the road and stop.,d:Only on highways.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches using lights and siren, you must yield the right-of-way by pulling as close as safely possible to the right edge of the road and stopping until it has passed. This applies whether the vehicle is coming from behind you, toward you, or from a side street. The only common exception is when you are in a divided highway and the emergency vehicle is on the opposite side with a physical barrier between you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which maneuver is allowed from a center left-turn lane?
options: a:You may pass slow-moving traffic.,b:You may make left turns.,c:You may make U-turns where U-turns are legal and it is safe to do so.
note: A center left‑turn lane is a shared lane used only for preparing and making left turns from either direction; it is not a passing lane and not for continuous driving. In many states, you may also use this lane to start a permitted U‑turn when it is legal and safe, but you must never use it to pass other vehicles or to travel long distances.

question: Seat belts are most effective when worn by:
options: a:The person driving the car.,b:Passengers only on long trips.,c:All occupants of the vehicle.,d:Only occupants in the front seats.
note: Make sure every person in the vehicle wears a seat belt—unrestrained occupants can be seriously injured and become hazards to others in a crash.

question: Which of the following will help a person sober up after drinking alcohol?
options: a:Hot coffee,b:Tomato juice and lime,c:Fresh air,d:Allowing enough time to pass
note: Only time can reduce your blood alcohol concentration. Coffee, food, cold showers, or fresh air might make you feel more awake, but they do not speed up how fast your body processes alcohol. You must wait long enough for your body to eliminate the alcohol before driving.

question: What does a flashing yellow X lane-use signal mean?
options: a:This lane may be used only for left turns.,b:The signal is about to change to a red X.,c:The signal is about to change to a green arrow.
note: Lane-use control signals manage which lanes you may use. A flashing yellow X over a lane means that lane is for left turns only. You must not drive straight through in that lane; use it only to make a left turn when it is safe.

question: What is the best way to handle a tailgater?
options: a:Slam on your brakes to get the other driver to back off.,b:Speed up to increase the distance between you and the tailgater.,c:Change lanes or gradually slow down to allow them to pass.
note: When another driver is following too closely, the safest response is to create space, not to speed up or brake suddenly. Gradually slow down and, when it is safe, change lanes or otherwise allow the tailgater to pass. This reduces the risk of a rear-end collision and keeps you in better control of the situation.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an intersection ahead is blocked by traffic, what should you do?
options: a:Get as close as possible to the car in front of you.,b:Go slowly until the traffic ahead moves.,c:Stay out of the intersection until you can completely pass through.
note: You must not enter an intersection unless there is enough space on the other side for your vehicle to completely clear it. If traffic ahead is stopped and would force you to stop in the intersection, wait behind the stop line until you can pass all the way through without blocking cross traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does the driver's left arm extended upward signal mean?
options: a:The driver intends to turn right.,b:The driver intends to turn left.,c:The driver is coming to a stop.
note: Standard hand signals are: left arm straight out for a left turn, left arm bent upward at the elbow for a right turn, and left arm bent downward for slowing or stopping. A left arm extended upward tells others you intend to turn right, which is useful if your turn signals are not working.

question: Do large vehicles have blind spots that can extend up to 200 feet behind them?
options: a:TRUE,b:FALSE
note: Large trucks and buses have large blind spots, called no-zones, directly behind them that can extend up to about 200 feet. If you follow too closely, the driver may not see you, and you will have less time and space to react if the truck stops suddenly.

question: What describes an inattentive driver?
options: a:Someone who daydreams or stares off the roadway while driving.,b:Someone who maintains eye contact during a conversation with a passenger.,c:Someone who only watches the vehicle ahead.
note: An inattentive driver is not fully focused on the driving task, such as daydreaming, staring off the roadway, or focusing on passengers or scenery instead of traffic. This includes maintaining eye contact with a passenger during conversation or only watching the vehicle ahead instead of scanning the whole traffic scene. Good drivers constantly scan the road, mirrors, and surroundings and avoid mental and visual distractions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about speed is correct?
options: a:Driving too slowly on some highways can be dangerous.,b:Speeding can be fatal.,c:Speeding is not dangerous for skilled drivers.,d:Both A and B
note: Driving much slower than the flow of traffic can cause sudden braking and lane changes, increasing the risk of crashes. Speeding is also dangerous because higher speeds greatly increase stopping distance and crash severity, and even skilled drivers cannot overcome the laws of physics. Safe drivers travel at a speed that is legal and appropriate for conditions.

question: What does an advisory speed sign attached to a curve sign indicate?
options: a:A recommended speed for the curve that should be reduced further in poor conditions.,b:A sign that may be ignored in rain or snow.,c:A blue sign with black lettering.
note: An advisory speed sign under a curve sign shows the recommended maximum speed for that curve in ideal conditions. It is not a mandatory speed limit, but you should treat it seriously and slow down. In rain, snow, or other poor conditions, you should reduce your speed even further below the advisory speed to maintain control.

question: What do fluorescent yellow-green traffic signs usually indicate?
options: a:Pedestrian, bicycle, and school warning areas.,b:Hospitals ahead.,c:Speed limits.
note: Fluorescent yellow-green signs are used for pedestrian crossings, bicycle crossings, and school-related warnings. When you see these signs, expect people walking or biking, or children near the roadway, and be prepared to slow down and stop if necessary.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you're driving so slowly that traffic is backing up behind you on a two-lane, two-way road, what should you do?
options: a:Pull off to the right and let traffic pass.,b:Decrease your speed further.,c:Refuse to let other cars pass.
note: On a two-lane, two‑way road, if you are moving so slowly that traffic is building up behind you, you should safely pull off to the right when possible and let the backed‑up vehicles pass. This reduces driver frustration and lowers the risk of unsafe passing maneuvers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you drive in a lane displaying a red X lane-use signal?
options: a:If you are passing the car in front of you.,b:If there is no visible oncoming traffic.,c:Never.
note: A red X lane‑use signal means that lane is closed to traffic in your direction. You must never drive in, enter, or stay in a lane with a red X above it, regardless of traffic conditions.

question: A double solid yellow line at the center of a two-lane road indicates:
options: a:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to pass.,b:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are not permitted to pass.,c:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are permitted to pass when it is safe to do so.
note: A double solid yellow line in the center of a two‑lane road separates traffic moving in opposite directions and means no passing is allowed from either direction. You may cross it only when turning left into or out of a driveway or side road, if it is safe and not otherwise prohibited.

question: What should drivers do to following distance when driving in bad weather?
options: a:Decrease their following distance.,b:Increase their following distance.,c:Maintain the normal following distance.,d:Follow as close as possible to help other drivers.
note: In bad weather such as rain, snow, fog, or icy conditions, you should increase your following distance. Extra space gives you more time to see hazards, react, and stop safely on slippery or low‑visibility roads.

question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights or hear its siren, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down but remain in your lane.,b:Keep driving in your lane and ignore it.,c:Pull to the right curb or side of the road and stop.,d:Speed up to get out of its way.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing lights or siren, you must yield the right‑of‑way by pulling as close as you safely can to the right curb or edge of the road and stopping until it has passed, unless directed otherwise by a police officer.

question: If your vehicle's accelerator becomes stuck while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Turn on your four-way flashers.,b:Slam on your brakes.,c:Sound your horn and continue driving.,d:Shift to neutral, steer smoothly, apply the brakes, and move safely off the road; then turn off the ignition once you are under control.
note: If the accelerator sticks, keep calm, shift to neutral to disconnect engine power from the wheels, then steer smoothly while applying firm, steady brake pressure. Once you have control and are moving to the side of the road, you may turn off the ignition, being careful not to lock the steering. Bring the vehicle to a complete stop in a safe place and turn on your hazard lights.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a narrow road when you meet an oncoming vehicle, you must:
options: a:Pull completely off the road and stop.,b:Allow the oncoming vehicle at least one-half of the main-traveled portion of the road.,c:Demand the other vehicle pull over to make room.,d:Stop and flash your lights.
note: On a narrow two-way road, each driver must share the available pavement so both vehicles can pass safely. You should keep as far to the right as is safe and allow the oncoming vehicle at least one-half of the main-traveled portion of the roadway. Do not force the other driver off the road or insist on having more than your share of the lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which signal requires you to come to a full stop, yield, and then proceed when clear?
options: a:A solid green light.,b:A flashing yellow light.,c:A flashing red light.,d:A solid red light.
note: A flashing red light is treated the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop at the stop line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection, yield to pedestrians and other traffic, and then proceed only when the way is clear and it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on an interstate, what should you do?
options: a:Stop and make a U-turn on the interstate.,b:Continue to the next exit and safely return.,c:Back up in your lane to reach the exit.,d:Signal and cross the median to return to the exit.
note: If you miss your exit on an interstate, keep going to the next exit. Do not stop, back up, make a U-turn, or cross the median. Instead, exit at the next opportunity, then use the proper ramps or roads to return to your intended route safely.

question: Is it legal to drive through, around, or under a railroad crossing gate or barrier?
options: a:True,b:False
note: It is illegal and extremely dangerous to drive through, around, or under a lowered railroad gate or barrier. You must stop when the gates are down or lights are flashing and remain stopped until the signals stop and the gates are fully raised, then proceed only when you are sure the tracks are clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you see a steady yellow signal, how should you respond?
options: a:Accelerate to avoid a red light.,b:Continue driving, as you have the right-of-way.,c:Slow to a stop unless you are already within the intersection.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. You must prepare to stop and stop if you can do so safely before the intersection. If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, continue through and clear the intersection; do not stop in the middle.

question: A flashing yellow traffic light means:
options: a:Stop and wait for a green light.,b:Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down and proceed with caution. You do not have to stop, but you must be prepared to yield to pedestrians or other vehicles already in or approaching the intersection if they have the right-of-way.

question: Which is NOT a primary factor in stopping distance?
options: a:Braking distance,b:Reaction distance,c:Steering ability,d:Perception distance
note: Total stopping distance is made up of perception distance, reaction distance, and braking distance. Perception distance is how far you travel from the moment you see a hazard until your brain recognizes it. Reaction distance is how far you travel while moving your foot to the brake. Braking distance is how far the vehicle travels after you apply the brakes until it stops. Steering ability affects how you avoid hazards, but it is not one of the components used to calculate stopping distance.

question: When a traffic signal light turns green, what must you do first?
options: a:Accelerate as quickly as possible.,b:Back up slowly.,c:Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians.
note: A green light means you may go only after you first yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and any vehicles still in the intersection. Even with a green signal, you must not enter the intersection until it is clear and safe.

question: Before backing up, what should you do?
options: a:Check behind your vehicle before getting in and use mirrors and look back while backing.,b:Depend entirely on your mirrors.,c:Accelerate quickly when backing up.
note: Before backing, walk around or look behind your vehicle to check for children, pedestrians, or obstacles you cannot see from the driver’s seat. Once in the vehicle, use your mirrors and turn your head to look through the rear window while backing slowly. Never rely only on mirrors or cameras when reversing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When two vehicles arrive at an intersection at the same time, which driver must yield?
options: a:Either driver may proceed.,b:The driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.,c:The driver on the right must yield to the driver on the left.,d:The larger vehicle must yield.
note: When two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This right‑of‑way rule helps prevent confusion and collisions by giving a clear priority to the vehicle on the right.

question: Which action reduces the risk of hydroplaning?
options: a:Driving through shallow water.,b:Driving more slowly.,c:Driving more quickly.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on a thin layer of water and lose contact with the road. The faster you drive on a wet surface, the more likely you are to hydroplane. Slowing down, especially in heavy rain or standing water, greatly reduces this risk.

question: Which of the following commonly causes traffic accidents?
options: a:Inattentive driving.,b:Driving too fast for conditions.,c:Following too closely.,d:All of the above.
note: Many crashes are caused by driver behavior. Not paying attention, driving too fast for road or weather conditions, and following other vehicles too closely all increase the chance of a collision. Because each of these is a common cause, the correct choice is that all of them contribute to accidents.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When are hand and arm signals permitted instead of mechanical turn signals?
options: a:At night,b:During daylight hours,c:When driving a loaded vehicle that blocks hand signals,d:When passing on a two-lane road
note: Hand and arm signals are allowed during daylight when your signals are not working or are hard to see. They must be clearly visible to other drivers, so you should not rely on them at night or when your arm cannot be seen, such as with certain loads or vehicle designs.

question: What do your brake lights signal to other drivers?
options: a:Are making a turn.,b:Are slowing down or stopping.,c:Are changing lanes.
note: Brake lights warn drivers behind you that you are slowing down or stopping. This gives them time to reduce speed and maintain a safe following distance, helping to prevent rear‑end collisions.

question: Which factors affect braking distance?
options: a:Vehicle speed, condition of brakes and tires, and pavement condition.,b:The time of day only.,c:Presence of signal lights only.
note: Braking distance increases with higher speed, worn or poorly adjusted brakes, worn tires, and slippery or uneven pavement. Good brakes and tires and dry, clean pavement help shorten the distance needed to stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless otherwise posted, the speed limit in an urban or town area is:
options: a:45 mph.,b:30 mph.,c:55 mph.
note: In many states, the default speed limit in business or residential (urban) areas is 25–30 mph when not otherwise posted. For a generic test, 30 mph is commonly used as the standard urban/town default limit unless signs show a different speed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In which situations are drivers required to stop their vehicles?
options: a:At stop signs, red lights, or when ordered by a traffic officer.,b:Only at stop signs.,c:Only when a traffic officer orders a stop.
note: You must come to a complete stop at stop signs, at red traffic lights (unless a specific sign or signal allows movement), and any time a police officer or other authorized person directs you to stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing an emergency vehicle stopped on the roadside, which action is required?
options: a:Vacate the nearest lane or slow down if you cannot safely move over.,b:Increase your speed to get past quickly.,c:Pull off behind the stopped vehicle and wait.
note: When you see an emergency, tow, or service vehicle stopped with flashing lights, you must move over one lane away if it is safe. If you cannot safely change lanes, you must slow down significantly and pass with extra caution.

question: When sharing the road with a truck, remember trucks generally:
options: a:Require longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles do.,b:Require less time to pass on a downgrade than smaller vehicles do.,c:Require a smaller turning radius than smaller vehicles do.,d:Always travel slower uphill
note: Large trucks are much heavier than passenger cars, so they need more distance to come to a complete stop. Always leave extra space in front of a truck and avoid cutting in too closely, especially when traffic is slowing or stopping.

question: What greatly increases stopping distances and crash severity?
options: a:Slow speeds.,b:Night drives.,c:High speeds.
note: Higher speeds mean your vehicle travels farther during your reaction time and needs more distance for the brakes to stop it. Speed also increases the force of impact in a crash, which makes damage and injuries much more severe.

question: A sign stating 'Reduced speed 35 mph' means what?
options: a:That the new 35 mph speed limit begins at the next speed limit sign.,b:That the new 35 mph speed limit begins at this sign.,c:That you have plenty of time to slow before the reduced speed zone.
note: A “Reduced speed 35 mph” sign means the new 35 mph limit starts at that sign. You should already be slowing so that by the time you reach the sign, you are at or below 35 mph.

question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means:
options: a:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the solid line.,b:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the broken line.,c:Passing on the left is permitted from either direction.
note: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means only the traffic next to the broken line may pass when it is safe. Traffic next to the solid line must not cross it to pass.

question: How should you check your vehicle's blind spots?
options: a:By turning your head and looking over your shoulders.,b:By looking in your side mirrors.,c:By looking in your rearview mirror.
note: Mirrors do not show areas directly alongside and slightly behind your vehicle, called blind spots. Before changing lanes or merging, quickly turn your head and look over your shoulder to check these areas.

question: Is it lawful to drive alongside a motorcycle in the same lane?
options: a:False — you must never share a lane with a motorcycle.,b:True
note: Motorcycles are entitled to a full lane, just like any other vehicle. Do not drive side‑by‑side with a motorcycle in the same lane; it reduces their space to maneuver and increases the risk of a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning or changing lanes, when must you signal?
options: a:Always signal your intentions, even if no traffic is visible.,b:Only signal if other traffic is present.,c:Only signal at night.,d:Signal only when turning right.
note: You must always signal before turning, changing lanes, or pulling away from the curb, even if you do not see other traffic. Signaling is required by law and gives other road users time to react to your movements.

question: What does a single dashed yellow centerline indicate?
options: a:Drivers may not pass.,b:Both lanes travel in the same direction.,c:Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.
note: A single dashed yellow centerline separates traffic moving in opposite directions. When the line is dashed on your side, you may cross it to pass another vehicle if you can do so safely and without interfering with oncoming traffic.

question: If a bicyclist disobeys traffic laws, what can occur?
options: a:Is in the right because bicyclists don’t have to obey traffic laws.,b:Can be ticketed.,c:Will always receive a warning from law enforcement.
note: Bicyclists on the road generally have the same rights and responsibilities as drivers of motor vehicles. If they disobey traffic laws—such as running red lights or stop signs—they can be stopped and ticketed by law enforcement.

question: What is the purpose of highway markings?
options: a:Are usually not important.,b:Are only found in construction zones.,c:Provide information for drivers.
note: Highway and pavement markings provide important information, such as lane boundaries, passing zones, turn lanes, and warnings about upcoming conditions. Drivers must understand and obey these markings to travel safely and legally.

question: When approaching a disabled pedestrian using a guide dog or white cane, what must you do?
options: a:You must always yield the right-of-way and use extra caution.,b:You only yield if they are in a marked crosswalk.
note: Yield the right-of-way to disabled pedestrians who use assistive devices; they are entitled to the same protections as all pedestrians.

question: What does a solid yellow arrow indicate?
options: a:Arrows are never used,b:It has the same meaning as a circular yellow traffic light—you must prepare to stop,c:Drivers may turn in the direction indicated by the arrow,d:It applies only to buses
note: A solid yellow arrow means the protected turning movement is ending. You should slow down and prepare to stop because the signal will soon change to red. If you are already in the intersection and cannot stop safely, you may complete the turn, but you should not enter the intersection expecting continued protection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection together, who must yield?
options: a:The largest vehicle.,b:The car on the left must yield to the car on the right.,c:The car on the right must yield.,d:The vehicle with the highest speed must yield.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection where two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This right‑of‑way rule helps prevent confusion and collisions when there are no signs or signals.

question: If another driver cuts you off in traffic, what is the safest response?
options: a:Let it go.,b:Pull up alongside and yell at them.,c:Flash your high beams at the driver.,d:Follow them closely to teach them a lesson.
note: If another driver cuts you off, the safest response is to stay calm, avoid eye contact or gestures, and let the incident go. Create extra space if needed and continue driving defensively. Reacting aggressively increases the risk of a crash and road rage.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes on a multilane highway, what should you do?
options: a:Turn on your headlights.,b:Signal, check your mirrors, and check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.,c:Sound your horn.
note: Before changing lanes, always signal, check your mirrors, and then look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move. This head check lets you see into your blind spot, where another vehicle may be hidden from your mirrors.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a highway from an entrance ramp, you should generally:
options: a:Accelerate to match the speed of traffic on the highway and merge when safe.,b:Enter slowly to avoid other vehicles.,c:Stop at the end of the ramp, then slowly enter traffic.,d:Drive on the shoulder to enter traffic.
note: When using an entrance ramp, use the acceleration lane to reach the speed of traffic on the highway, signal, and merge when there is a safe gap. Entering too slowly or stopping at the end of the ramp can surprise other drivers and increase the risk of a collision.

question: At night, which is hardest to see?
options: a:Other motorists.,b:Road signs.,c:Pedestrians.
note: Pedestrians are usually the hardest to see at night because they are smaller, often wear dark clothing, and may not be in well‑lit areas. Headlights and reflective materials make other vehicles and road signs much more visible than people on or near the roadway.

question: When stopped for a traffic violation or equipment check, which documents must the driver produce?
options: a:Proof of insurance only.,b:Driver's license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance.,c:Proof of registration only.,d:Only their driver's license and insurance card.
note: When an officer stops you, you are generally required to show your driver’s license, the vehicle’s registration, and proof of financial responsibility (insurance). These documents show that you are legally licensed to drive, that the vehicle is properly registered, and that you have insurance coverage.

question: Is it ever acceptable to drive around or under a railroad crossing gate that is being lowered or raised?
options: a:If your vehicle can do so without damaging the gate.,b:Under no circumstances.,c:If you first look carefully in both directions.,d:As long as an approaching train is not too close.
note: You must never drive around, under, or through a railroad crossing gate that is moving or down, even if you do not see a train. Flashing lights, bells, and lowered gates mean a train is approaching or nearby, and trains cannot stop quickly. Wait until the gates are fully raised and the signals stop before proceeding.

question: Anything that requires you to ____ could cause you to crash.
options: a:Take your hands off the wheel,b:Take your attention away from the task of driving.,c:Take your eyes off the road.
note: Anything that takes your attention away from the task of driving can cause a crash. Distractions include taking your eyes off the road, your hands off the wheel, or your mind off driving. Even if your hands stay on the wheel, mental or visual distractions can be just as dangerous.

question: When driving through an area where children are playing, you should expect them to:
options: a:Know when it is safe to cross the street.,b:Stop at the curb before crossing the street.,c:Run out into the street without looking,d:Always stay on the sidewalk.
note: Children are unpredictable and may run into the street without looking for traffic. When driving where children are playing, slow down, cover the brake, and be prepared to stop suddenly because they may not understand traffic dangers or follow safety rules.

question: When roads may be slippery, what should you avoid doing?
options: a:Always drive at the maximum speed limit.,b:Use cruise control to maintain a steady speed.,c:Reduce your following distance.
note: On slippery roads you should slow down, increase your following distance, and avoid using cruise control so you can react quickly if your tires lose traction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Do you have to signal every time you pull away from a curb?
options: a:True,b:False
note: You must signal any time you pull away from a curb so other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians know you are about to enter the traffic lane.

question: A pentagonal (five-sided) traffic sign usually warns of what?
options: a:A no-passing zone ahead.,b:A school zone or school crossing.,c:A speed limit change.,d:A railroad crossing.
note: Five‑sided (pentagon) signs indicate school zones and school crossings, warning you to slow down and watch carefully for children.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the correct action when approaching a roundabout?
options: a:Decrease your speed and be prepared to yield.,b:Maintain your speed.,c:Increase your speed to enter quickly.
note: When approaching a roundabout, slow down, be prepared to yield to traffic already in the circle and to pedestrians, and enter only when there is a safe gap.

question: Which factor does NOT affect blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Your body weight.,b:How much time passes between drinks.,c:The type of alcoholic beverage you drink.,d:How much you drink.
note: BAC is mainly affected by how much alcohol you consume, your body weight, and how quickly you drink it; the type of alcoholic beverage does not change BAC if the total amount of alcohol is the same.

question: What do work zone signs indicate?
options: a:Less-than-ideal driving conditions and nearby road work.,b:That it is summer.,c:You must immediately stop and back up.
note: Work zone signs are orange and warn that road work, workers, or equipment are on or near the roadway. They tell you that conditions may be changing or hazardous, so you should slow down, be alert, and use extra caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does the driver's left arm and hand extended downward signal?
options: a:Turn left.,b:Turn right.,c:Stop or slow down.
note: Hand signals are used if turn signals are not working or not visible. Left arm straight out means a left turn, left arm bent up means a right turn, and left arm extended downward means the driver intends to stop or slow down. When you see the arm down signal, be ready to reduce speed or stop.

question: Which winter driving statement is not true?
options: a:Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.,b:Winter is the most difficult driving season.,c:Check antifreeze and washer fluid levels frequently in winter.
note: In winter, roads can be icy or snowy and traction is reduced, so using cruise control is unsafe because it can cause you to lose control if the wheels slip. Winter is generally the most difficult driving season, and you should check antifreeze and washer fluid often to keep your vehicle operating safely.

question: When must you stop for a school bus on a two-lane highway?
options: a:Only if the bus is on your side of the road.,b:Only if you see children crossing.,c:When the bus's red lights are flashing and it is stopped to load or unload children.,d:Never, if you are in a vehicle with seat belts.
note: On a two-lane road, traffic in both directions must stop when a school bus is stopped with red lights flashing to load or unload children. You must remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and the bus starts moving or the driver signals you to proceed.

question: At dusk or on overcast days, what lighting should you use?
options: a:Four-way hazard flashers.,b:Parking lights only.,c:Headlights (low beams) when appropriate.,d:No lights are necessary.
note: Turn on headlights at dusk or on overcast days; use low beams within 1,000 feet of oncoming vehicles and within 500 feet of a vehicle you are following.

question: If a school bus is stopped with red lights flashing on a private road, must you stop?
options: a:True — you must stop.,b:False
note: School‑bus laws generally apply on public roads. On many private roads or parking lots, the specific statute requiring all traffic to stop for a school bus with flashing red lights does not apply, though you should still use extreme caution and be prepared to stop for children. Always check your state law, but in general you are not automatically required by statute to stop on private property the same way you are on public streets.

question: When is it appropriate to honk your horn?
options: a:When passing a bicyclist.,b:When traveling through an intersection.,c:When you see a child who is about to run into the street.
note: Use your horn only as a warning to help prevent a collision, such as when a child or pedestrian is about to step into the street and may not see you. Do not honk just because you are passing a bicyclist or driving through an intersection; unnecessary horn use can startle others and is often illegal.

question: Which of the following is important to remember when driving on wet pavement?
options: a:The road is most slippery just after it starts to rain.,b:Hydroplaning cannot occur if you reduce speed.,c:You need no extra space when stopping.,d:Stand on the brakes to drive through puddles.
note: When it first starts to rain, water mixes with oil and dirt on the road, making the surface especially slippery. Slow down, increase your following distance, and avoid sudden braking or sharp turns. Hydroplaning can still occur at higher speeds even if you slow somewhat, so the safest approach is to reduce speed significantly and drive smoothly on wet pavement.

question: What is the only effective way to reduce your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Allow your body time to get rid of the alcohol.,b:Drink coffee.,c:Exercise.
note: Time is the only reliable way for the body to lower BAC; coffee, exercise, or cold showers do not reduce BAC.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a freeway you should:
options: a:Signal, yield to existing traffic, and enter at the same speed that traffic is moving.,b:Signal and enter the freeway. Freeway traffic must yield.,c:Drive slowly so you can check traffic.
note: When entering a freeway, use the entrance ramp and acceleration lane to match the speed of traffic, signal early, and yield to vehicles already on the freeway. Merge only when there is a safe gap. Entering too slowly can disrupt traffic and increase the risk of a collision, and freeway traffic is not required to yield to you.

question: How does alcohol affect your reflexes and judgment?
options: a:Is most pronounced when consuming hard ciders and mixed drinks.,b:Depends on how much alcohol is in the bloodstream.,c:Is less pronounced when consuming beer instead of wine.
note: Alcohol affects your brain and nervous system based on how much alcohol is in your bloodstream (your BAC), not on whether you drank beer, wine, or liquor. As BAC rises, your judgment, reaction time, and coordination get worse, increasing crash risk even at relatively low levels.

question: On slippery roads, what is the recommended action regarding speed?
options: a:Drive more quickly.,b:Drive the posted speed limit with caution.,c:Slow down.
note: On slippery roads from rain, snow, or ice, you must slow down, often to a speed below the posted limit. Reduced traction means it takes longer to stop and easier to lose control, so lowering your speed gives you more time and space to react safely.

question: If you are following a school bus or a large tank truck, what should you be prepared to do at railroad crossings?
options: a:Pass them on the right.,b:Be prepared to stop at all railroad crossings.,c:Expect them to speed up.,d:Sound your horn to get them to move.
note: Many school buses and certain tank trucks carrying hazardous materials are required by law to stop at all railroad crossings. When following them, leave extra space and be ready to stop as they approach the tracks, even if the signals are not active.

question: True or False: Talking or texting on a cell phone while driving will not significantly increase your crash risk.
options: a:FALSE,b:TRUE,c:Only if using hands-free,d:Depends on the driver's experience
note: The statement is false because any talking or texting on a cell phone while driving significantly increases crash risk. Phone use takes your eyes, mind, or hands away from driving, slowing your reactions and making it easier to miss hazards or drift from your lane.

question: When parallel parking, how far from the curb should your vehicle be?
options: a:No more than 10 inches.,b:No more than 12 inches.,c:No more than 18 inches.,d:No more than 24 inches.
note: When parallel parked, your vehicle should be no more than 12 inches from the curb. Parking close to the curb keeps you out of moving traffic while still leaving enough space so you do not hit or scrape the curb when entering or leaving the space.

question: To ensure your physical condition won't impair driving, what should you do?
options: a:Keep physically fit and have routine physical exams.,b:Know how any medication affects your driving, and drive within your limits.,c:Ignore minor health issues until after driving.,d:Both a and b.
note: Your physical condition directly affects your driving. Staying physically fit and getting regular checkups helps detect problems that could interfere with safe driving. You must also know how any medications you take affect alertness, vision, and coordination, and always drive within your physical limits.

question: Which statement is true about adjusting driving for weather?
options: a:You should slow down when driving in rain and fog.,b:Be particularly aware of vehicles coming up behind you in inclement weather.,c:A sudden change in weather calls for a change in driving.,d:All of the above.
note: In bad weather you must adjust your driving to conditions. This usually means slowing down in rain, snow, or fog, increasing following distance, and being especially alert to traffic around you, including vehicles approaching from behind. Any sudden change in weather is a signal to change how you drive, not to keep driving the same way.

question: Is the most common mistake when backing up failing to look both ways behind you?
options: a:True,b:False
note: When backing, many crashes happen because drivers fail to look carefully in both directions behind the vehicle. Mirrors alone do not show the full area; you should turn your head and body to look through the rear window and check all around before and while backing.

question: Which of the following is an effect of alcohol on driving?
options: a:It gives you a feeling of false confidence.,b:It impairs your thinking ability.,c:It slows your reaction time.,d:All of the above.
note: Alcohol affects several driving abilities at the same time. It slows your reaction time, makes your thinking and judgment less reliable, and often gives a false sense of confidence so you take risks you normally would avoid. Because all of these effects are dangerous, you should never drive after drinking.

question: Do ramps and bridges freeze before roadways?
options: a:True — ramps and bridges can freeze quicker and need extra caution.,b:False
note: Bridges and ramps freeze before the rest of the roadway because cold air surrounds them from above and below, allowing ice to form more quickly. Even if the main road looks just wet, elevated structures may be icy, so reduce speed and use extra caution when crossing them in cold weather.

question: When stopped in a line of traffic at a railroad crossing with no signals, what must you ensure?
options: a:There is enough space to clear the tracks so you won't stop on them.,b:You have the right-of-way and do not need to check for trains.,c:You may pass slower drivers while crossing the track.
note: Before you cross railroad tracks, you must be sure there is enough room on the far side so your entire vehicle can clear the tracks without stopping. Never stop on the tracks, and never pass other vehicles near a crossing. Always look and listen for trains, even if there are no signals.

question: When entering interstate traffic from an entrance or acceleration ramp, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:You have the right-of-way and may force your way in.,b:You should yield to drivers already on the interstate.,c:You must come to a full stop at the end of the ramp.,d:You may drive on the shoulder to merge.
note: When entering an interstate, you must yield to traffic already on the highway. Use the entrance or acceleration ramp to match the speed of traffic, signal, and merge only when there is a safe gap. Do not force your way in, stop unnecessarily at the end of the ramp, or drive on the shoulder to merge.

question: A railroad crossbuck sign should be treated the same as which traffic control?
options: a:A crossbuck is treated like a stop sign.,b:A crossbuck is treated like a yield sign.
note: A railroad crossbuck sign is treated like a yield sign, not like a stop sign or traffic light. You must slow, look, and listen for trains and be prepared to stop. If a train is approaching, you must yield the right‑of‑way and stop well before the tracks; if no train is coming and it is safe, you may proceed without stopping.

question: When a school bus is stopped on the opposite side of a multilane highway separated by a median, drivers:
options: a:Must stop and wait for the flashing lights to stop.,b:Must stop until the bus begins moving.,c:Must stop until the stop arm is lifted.,d:May continue driving without stopping.
note: On a multilane highway that has a physical median or divider, drivers traveling on the opposite side from a stopped school bus with red lights flashing generally do not have to stop. When there is no median or divider, traffic in both directions must stop for a school bus with red lights flashing and remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and it is safe to proceed, as required by state law.

question: What does an \End school zone\" sign indicate?"
options: a:The school zone reduced speed limit has ended.,b:The start of a 20 mph school speed zone.,c:Increased danger of encountering children ahead.,d:A required stop for school buses only.
note: An “End school zone” sign tells you that the reduced speed limit for the school zone has ended. After passing this sign, you may resume driving at the regular posted speed limit for that roadway, but you must never exceed the speed shown on the sign.

question: Does drinking coffee after consuming alcohol reduce your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Has no effect on blood alcohol concentration.,b:Decreases blood alcohol concentration.,c:Cancels the effect of the alcohol.
note: Time is the only thing that lowers your blood alcohol concentration. Coffee, cold showers, exercise, or fresh air might make you feel more awake, but they do not speed up how fast your body removes alcohol. You are still impaired until your body has had enough time to process the alcohol.

question: Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings must be:
options: a:Are merely suggestions.,b:Must always be obeyed.,c:Must be followed only when there is other traffic.
note: Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings are legal traffic control devices and must always be obeyed. They are not suggestions; they are there to organize traffic flow, prevent crashes, and protect all road users.

question: How serious is drinking and driving as a traffic safety problem?
options: a:A minor traffic safety problem.,b:A serious traffic safety problem.,c:Safe if you have only had a few drinks.
note: Drinking and driving is a major cause of serious and fatal crashes. Even a small amount of alcohol can slow your reaction time and affect judgment, making it a serious traffic safety problem with severe legal and safety consequences.

question: Where is it best to keep a space cushion around your vehicle?
options: a:Only in back of your vehicle.,b:On all sides of your vehicle.,c:Only in front of the vehicle.
note: A space cushion on all sides of your vehicle gives you room to react and maneuver if another driver makes a mistake or a hazard appears. Extra space in front, behind, and to the sides reduces the chance of collisions and allows safer lane changes and stops.

question: At night when an oncoming vehicle approaches, which headlight setting should you use?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Parking lights only.
note: When another vehicle is approaching at night, you must use low beam headlights so you do not blind the other driver. High beams are only for use when there is no oncoming traffic and you are not closely following another vehicle.

question: Are drivers required to yield to children playing in the street?
options: a:True — you must always drive with extreme caution where children may be present.,b:False — you must use extreme caution and be prepared to stop, but children playing in the street do not automatically have the legal right-of-way.
note: You must always drive with extreme caution where children may be present, but children playing in the street do not have the legal right‑of‑way over vehicles. The law requires drivers to slow, be prepared to stop, and avoid hitting any pedestrian, but it does not say you must automatically yield to children who are unlawfully in the roadway. Safest practice is to slow way down and stop if needed, but the legal right‑of‑way still follows normal pedestrian rules.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following must you obey over signs, signals, and pavement markings?
options: a:A flashing yellow light.,b:A steady red light.,c:A police officer directing traffic.,d:A stop sign.
note: A police officer or other authorized person directing traffic always overrides traffic signals, signs, and pavement markings. If their hand signals or verbal directions conflict with a light or sign, you must follow the officer. This helps manage emergencies, crashes, or special events safely and efficiently.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When moving from the right lane into the left lane on a multilane highway, what should you do first?
options: a:Look in your rearview mirror for traffic behind you before changing lanes.,b:Look over your left shoulder for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes.,c:Look in your mirrors for traffic, turn on your directional signal, then check your blind spot before changing lanes.
note: Before moving into another lane, you should first check traffic using your mirrors and signal your intention so other drivers know what you plan to do. After that, quickly look over your shoulder in the direction of the lane change to check your blind spot, then change lanes when it is safe. The blind‑spot check is critical, but it comes after you have checked mirrors and signaled.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a crowded freeway, what should you do?
options: a:Use the acceleration lane to adjust your speed to match freeway traffic.,b:Use your side and rearview mirrors and check your blind spots.,c:Yield to traffic already on the freeway.
note: When merging onto a freeway, use the acceleration lane to reach a speed that matches the flow of traffic, then find a safe gap. As you do this, check your mirrors and blind spots and be prepared to yield to vehicles already on the freeway. Freeway traffic has the right‑of‑way, so you must adjust your speed and position to merge safely without forcing others to brake suddenly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When arriving at a four-way stop, must you yield to drivers who reached the intersection before you?
options: a:No — you may proceed if the lane is clear.,b:Yes — yield to drivers who arrived earlier.,c:Only if they signal you to go.,d:Only if they are to your right.
note: At a four‑way stop, the basic rule is that the driver who arrives first has the right‑of‑way and should proceed first. If two or more vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right. Yielding to those who arrived before you keeps traffic moving in an orderly, predictable sequence and reduces confusion and crashes.

question: Why shouldn't you follow other cars too closely?
options: a:You might not see the road between vehicles.,b:You may not have time to stop if the vehicle ahead slows or stops suddenly.,c:You might not see the vehicle's turn signals.,d:All of the above.
note: Following too closely, or tailgating, is dangerous because you lose both visibility and reaction time. The vehicle ahead can block your view of the road and traffic conditions, and if it slows or stops suddenly you may not have enough space to brake safely. Keeping a safe following distance gives you time to see hazards, notice turn signals, and stop smoothly.

question: Why should drivers be especially alert for motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians?
options: a:Because they can be difficult to see and are more vulnerable in traffic.,b:They obey different traffic laws than vehicles.,c:They always have the right-of-way.
note: Motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians are smaller and can be hidden in blind spots or by other vehicles, so they are harder to see. They also have much less protection in a crash, so any collision is more likely to cause serious injury. Drivers must scan carefully, check mirrors and blind spots, and yield when required to protect these vulnerable road users.

question: What is the act of turning your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes called?
options: a:A good driving habit.,b:An unnecessary maneuver.,c:A bad driving habit.
note: Checking your blind spot by quickly turning your head before changing lanes is an essential safe‑driving habit. Mirrors do not show every area around your vehicle, so a brief head check helps you see vehicles, motorcycles, or bicycles that might be alongside you. Always signal, check mirrors, and then turn your head to check blind spots before moving into another lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is passing prohibited?
options: a:On hills and curves, at intersections, and at railroad crossings.,b:Only at intersections.,c:Only on hills.
note: Passing is prohibited where your view of oncoming traffic is limited or where conflicts are likely. On hills and curves, you cannot see far enough ahead to know if it is safe. At intersections and railroad crossings, other vehicles, trains, or pedestrians may enter your path. Road markings (solid lines) and signs will also indicate no‑passing zones in these areas.

question: Is alcohol the single greatest common factor in fatal motor vehicle crashes?
options: a:True — alcohol is the leading cause.,b:False — it is not a major factor.,c:True but only at night.,d:False — speeding is the leading cause.
note: Alcohol is a major factor in fatal crashes because it slows reaction time, reduces coordination, and impairs judgment. However, in recent national crash data, speeding is identified as the most frequent driver‑related factor in fatal motor vehicle crashes. Both speeding and impaired driving are extremely dangerous, and safe drivers avoid driving after drinking and always obey speed limits and adjust speed to conditions.

question: If you notice a vehicle defect that may affect safety, what should you do?
options: a:Correct the defect as soon as possible.,b:Drive the vehicle at slower speeds.,c:Correct the defect when you can afford it.
note: Any defect that could affect the safe operation of your vehicle—such as problems with brakes, tires, steering, or lights—should be repaired as soon as possible. Continuing to drive with a safety‑related defect increases the risk of a crash and can make you legally responsible if an accident occurs.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If waiting to turn left at a multilane intersection and opposing traffic blocks your view, what should you do?
options: a:Accelerate into the first clear lane and then cross the others.,b:Wait until you can clearly see all lanes you must cross before turning.,c:Proceed when a driver gestures you to go.,d:Edge forward into the intersection until the view clears.
note: When turning left across multiple lanes, you must not start your turn until you can clearly see that every lane you must cross is free of oncoming traffic, bicycles, and pedestrians. If your view is blocked, wait until it is completely clear; never rely on another driver’s signal or try to turn into a lane you cannot see.

question: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means:
options: a:Do not pass from your lane.,b:Pass with caution.,c:Slow down.
note: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means you may not legally pass other vehicles from your lane. It indicates that sight distance or other conditions make passing unsafe in your direction, so you must stay in your lane except when turning left where allowed.

question: If another driver is trying to pass you, how should you respond?
options: a:Maintain your lane and a steady speed; slightly reduce speed if needed so they can pass safely.,b:Signal when it is safe for them to pass and adjust speed so they can return to the lane.,c:Speed up to prevent them from passing.,d:Brake hard to block their pass.
note: When another driver is passing you, stay in your lane and maintain a steady speed so they can judge the distance needed to pass safely. If necessary, you may slightly reduce your speed to help them complete the pass, but you should never speed up, brake suddenly, or signal them that it is safe—only the passing driver is responsible for deciding when it is safe to pass.

question: What do crossbuck signs indicate?
options: a:No passing zones.,b:School zones.,c:Railroad crossings.
note: A crossbuck sign marks a railroad crossing. It functions like a yield sign: you must slow, look, and listen for trains, and be prepared to stop. You must yield the right‑of‑way to any approaching train and never stop on the tracks.

question: What does a red arrow on a traffic signal require drivers to do?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Stop and then proceed if the way is clear.,c:Stop and remain stopped until a green light or green arrow appears.,d:Turn only after signaling.
note: A red arrow means you must come to a complete stop and stay stopped. You may not go in the direction of the arrow until a green light or green arrow appears, unless a specific sign allows a turn on red.

question: Which of these does NOT typically happen after drinking alcohol?
options: a:Slowed reflexes and reaction time.,b:Distorted judgment of speed and distance.,c:Increased alertness.,d:Reduced ability to recover from glare.
note: Alcohol slows your reflexes, reduces alertness, distorts judgment of speed and distance, and makes it harder to recover from headlight glare. It does not increase alertness, so “increased alertness” is the effect that does NOT typically happen after drinking.

question: If a vehicle with anti-lock brakes (ABS) begins to lose traction on a slippery road, what should you do?
options: a:Press and hold the brake pedal and steer out of danger.,b:Pump the brakes manually.,c:Press and hold the accelerator.,d:Release the brake pedal immediately.
note: With ABS, press the brake pedal firmly and hold it; do not pump the brakes. The ABS system automatically pumps the brakes to prevent wheel lockup, allowing you to steer around hazards while maintaining as much control as possible.

question: If involved in a serious crash, what actions are required?
options: a:Stop, check for injuries, call 911 if anyone is injured, and report the crash to law enforcement when required.,b:Drive on if no one is injured.,c:Determine if anyone is injured before stopping.
note: In any crash, you must stop immediately, check for injuries, and stay at the scene. In a serious crash, call 911 if anyone is injured and, when required by law, report the collision to law enforcement. If possible and safe, move vehicles out of traffic to prevent further danger.

question: Which feature is used on some highways to direct drivers into the proper lanes for turning?
options: a:White lines on the side of the road,b:Flashing yellow lights,c:Arrow markings showing lane use,d:Flashing red lights
note: Arrow markings on the pavement or on overhead lane-use signs show which lanes are for turning left, turning right, or going straight. These markings help drivers get into the correct lane before reaching an intersection.

question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?
options: a:Not all railroad crossings are equipped with flashing red signals and gates.,b:You must stop at a railroad crossing when directed to do so by a flagger.,c:It is against the law to go around lowered gates.,d:All of the above.
note: Not all crossings have active warning devices like lights and gates, and it is illegal to go around lowered gates or ignore flaggers and signs.

question: What does a flashing red light in a traffic signal mean?
options: a:The same thing as a stop sign.,b:The traffic signal is broken.,c:You do not have to come to a complete stop.
note: A flashing red light means you must stop completely, yield to traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when it is safe, just as you would at a stop sign.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you signal before passing another vehicle?
options: a:Signal early enough for other drivers to be aware of your intention.,b:Signal just after you start changing lanes.,c:Signal only at intersections.,d:There is no need to signal when passing.
note: You should signal well in advance of changing lanes to pass so other drivers have time to see your signal and anticipate your movement.

question: What does a flashing yellow arrow for left turns mean?
options: a:Come to a complete stop before turning.,b:Merge into a lane in the arrow's direction.,c:You may turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,d:Left turns are prohibited.
note: A flashing yellow left-turn arrow means you may turn left, but you must first yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians and make the turn only when the way is clear.

question: When backing up, what is the safest technique to ensure you can see behind the vehicle?
options: a:Open the driver's door and look back while backing.,b:Rely only on your mirrors.,c:Turn your head and look through the rear window while backing.,d:Flash your lights while backing to warn pedestrians.
note: The safest way to back up is to turn your head and look directly through the rear window while moving slowly, after first checking behind the vehicle before you get in. Do not rely only on mirrors or cameras.

question: If your power steering fails while driving, what is the correct response?
options: a:Turn on your hazard lights and brace yourself.,b:Work harder to steer, reduce your speed, drive to a safe area, and stop.,c:Honk your horn and turn off the ignition.
note: If power steering fails, the vehicle will still steer, but it will require much more effort, especially at low speeds. Grip the wheel firmly, slow down, and carefully steer to the side of the road or another safe place. Once safely stopped, turn on your hazard lights if needed and arrange for the vehicle to be checked before driving again.

question: If you hit an unattended parked vehicle and the owner cannot be located, what must you do?
options: a:Must stay until the police arrive.,b:Have done as much as you can.,c:Leave a written notice with your name, address, and accident details.
note: If you hit a parked vehicle and cannot find the owner, you must stop, make a reasonable effort to locate them, and if you cannot, leave a written note in a secure, visible place. The note must include your name, address, and a brief description of what happened. In many states you are also required to report the collision to law enforcement, especially if there is significant damage.

question: If you are in another driver's blind spot, what should you do?
options: a:Stay in the driver's blind spot.,b:Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.,c:Keep a steady pace.
note: Blind spots are areas a driver cannot see in their mirrors. If you are traveling in another driver’s blind spot, they may change lanes or turn without realizing you are there. Either speed up to move ahead safely or slow down to fall back so you are clearly visible in their mirrors, and avoid lingering alongside other vehicles.

question: Is it legal to drive at night using only your parking lights?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Parking lights alone are not bright enough for safe night driving and do not meet legal headlight requirements. At night, and any time visibility is reduced (such as in rain, fog, or snow), you must use your headlights so you can see the road and other drivers can see you.

question: On a road with no sidewalks, which side should a pedestrian use?
options: a:Same side of the road on which traffic is moving.,b:Side of the road with the lightest traffic.,c:Side of the road facing oncoming traffic.
note: On roads without sidewalks, pedestrians should walk on the side of the road facing oncoming traffic. This allows pedestrians to see approaching vehicles and react if a driver drifts toward them, and it also makes them more visible to drivers.

question: Is smoking or preparing to smoke while driving distracting?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Handling cigarettes, lighters, or other smoking materials takes your hands and eyes off driving tasks and is a distraction.

question: Under which conditions must you stop at a railroad crossing?
options: a:Flashing red signals and gates are present and operating,b:Directed to do so by a flagger,c:It is controlled by a stop sign,d:Any of the above (flagger, stop sign, or active signals/gates)
note: You must stop when directed by a flagger, when a stop sign controls the crossing, or when flashing red signals and gates are active.

question: Under normal driving conditions, what following distance should drivers maintain?
options: a:Four seconds.,b:Three seconds.,c:Five seconds.
note: Use the three-second rule under normal conditions to maintain a safe following distance from the vehicle ahead.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you use your turn signals?
options: a:Changing lanes.,b:Pulling into or out of a parking space.,c:Pulling into traffic from a parking area or alley.,d:All of the above
note: Use turn signals whenever you make lateral movements or enter traffic so other road users know your intentions.

question: What does a single broken white line down the center of a two-lane road indicate?
options: a:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are permitted to pass when it is safe to do so.,b:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are permitted to pass when it is safe to do so.,c:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are not permitted to pass.,d:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to pass.
note: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A single broken white line indicates lane changes and passing are allowed when it is safe to do so.

question: Should you use high beam headlights while driving in fog?
options: a:FALSE,b:TRUE
