note: In fog, use low beam headlights or fog lights. High beams reflect off the water droplets in the fog and shine back at you, creating glare and making it harder to see the road and other vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When are you allowed to exceed the posted speed limit?
options: a:Never.,b:When legally passing another vehicle on a multilane highway with a posted speed limit of 55 mph or higher.,c:When there is no police officer present.,d:When traffic is light.
note: You must obey the posted speed limit. In general U.S. driving law, you are not allowed to exceed the posted limit, even when passing, when traffic is light, or when you do not see a police officer. Always adjust your speed to conditions, but stay at or below the posted limit unless a specific state law for that test says otherwise.

question: What is the “No zone” in relation to large trucks and buses?
options: a:Blind spots around a truck or bus where the vehicle cannot see you.,b:A special speed zone around trucks.,c:A roadway with restrictions on stereo volume.
note: The “No zone” is the large blind spot area around trucks and buses where the driver cannot see you in their mirrors. If you cannot see the truck driver’s mirrors, they likely cannot see you. Avoid staying in these areas, especially along the sides and directly behind the vehicle.

question: What do two solid yellow lines on the pavement indicate?
options: a:No passing in either direction.,b:Passing is allowed from both directions.,c:Passing allowed only at hilltops.
note: Two solid yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions and mean no passing from either direction. You must not cross them to pass another vehicle, though you may usually cross carefully to turn left into or out of a driveway or side road if it is safe and not otherwise prohibited.

question: Compared to smaller vehicles, do larger vehicles have larger blind spots?
options: a:Yes — larger vehicles have larger blind spots.,b:No — they have smaller blind spots.,c:No blind spots.
note: Larger vehicles such as trucks and buses have bigger blind spots than smaller vehicles. These blind spots are along both sides, directly behind, and sometimes directly in front of the vehicle. Stay out of these areas when possible so the driver can see you and react safely.

question: Lanes of traffic moving in the same direction are separated by which color lines?
options: a:Red,b:White,c:Yellow.
note: White lines (solid or broken) separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions, and red is not used to separate travel lanes.

question: Where are roads most likely to freeze quickly in cold/wet conditions?
options: a:Flat areas.,b:Shaded areas under trees or buildings.,c:Curvy sections.
note: Shaded areas under trees, bridges, or buildings freeze first and stay icy longer because they receive less sunlight. Even when other parts of the road look clear, shaded spots can still be slippery.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes, which is the correct practice?
options: a:Rely only on your mirrors.,b:Signal before changing lanes and check mirrors and blind spots.,c:Begin signaling as you move into the next lane.
note: Before changing lanes, you must signal, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. In many states you must signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes or turning in lower-speed areas, and at higher minimum distances on faster roads. Always signal before you start moving into the next lane, not while you are already moving over.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you do before turning left at an intersection?
options: a:Yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.,b:Sound your horn.,c:Swing to the right side of your lane.
note: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming vehicles, cyclists, and pedestrians in the crosswalk. Turn only when there is a safe gap and the path is clear.

question: When approaching an accident scene, what is the correct behavior?
options: a:Keep moving and maintain focus on your driving.,b:Stop if you are involved or if emergency help has not yet arrived.,c:Call the police immediately.
note: When approaching an accident scene, keep moving carefully and focus on your driving so you do not cause another crash. Only stop if you are directly involved or if emergency help has not yet arrived and you can safely assist.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left, to whom must you yield the right-of-way?
options: a:Oncoming traffic and pedestrians already in the intersection.,b:Only drivers who are already in the intersection.,c:No one — left turns always have right-of-way.
note: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming traffic that is close enough to be a hazard and to pedestrians already in the crosswalk or intersection. Only proceed when the way is clear and it is safe to complete your turn.

question: If a transit vehicle is signaling to re-enter the main roadway after stopping, what must you do?
options: a:Honk to tell the driver you are there.,b:Yield to the transit vehicle so it can safely re-enter traffic.,c:Speed up to block it from merging.,d:Ignore the signal and maintain your lane.
note: When a transit or bus driver signals to pull away from a stop and re-enter the lane, you must allow them to merge safely. Adjust by changing lanes, slowing, or stopping if needed so the larger vehicle can rejoin traffic without causing a collision.

question: If an approaching driver fails to dim their high-beam headlights, where should you look?
options: a:Directly into the headlights.,b:At the wheels of the approaching vehicle.,c:Toward the right side of the road and the edge of your lane.,d:Toward the left side of the road.
note: If an oncoming driver does not dim their high beams, avoid looking directly into the glare. Instead, glance toward the right side of the road and use the edge line or lane markings as a guide so you can stay in your lane while protecting your night vision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which actions are prohibited while stopped in a travel lane?
options: a:Stopping to drop off passengers or to check an address.,b:Stopping briefly to let someone out when traffic is light.,c:Backing up to reach an entrance ramp.,d:All of the above are prohibited.
note: Travel lanes are for moving traffic only. You must not stop in a travel lane to drop off passengers, check an address, or back up to reach a missed turn or ramp. If you miss an exit, continue to the next safe place to turn around rather than stopping or reversing in the lane.

question: What is the correct procedure when changing lanes or passing on an interstate?
options: a:Stop on the shoulder if you are tired.,b:Always use cruise control to maintain speed.,c:Signal, check mirrors, and check your blind spots before changing lanes.,d:Change lanes without signaling to be faster.
note: Before changing lanes or passing on an interstate, always signal, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check blind spots. Make sure the lane is clear and that you have enough space to move over safely; use the shoulder only for emergencies, not routine stops.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light at an intersection mean?
options: a:Continue normally through the intersection.,b:Slow down and proceed with care.,c:Stop and proceed when a green light appears.
note: A flashing yellow light means proceed with caution. You do not have to stop, but you must slow down, scan carefully for other vehicles, pedestrians, and hazards, and go through the intersection only when it is safe.

question: Is nighttime the safest time for cyclists to ride?
options: a:False — night riding is more hazardous.,b:True
note: Night riding is more dangerous for cyclists because they are harder for drivers to see, even with lights and reflectors. Both cyclists and drivers must be extra alert and use proper lighting and reflective gear after dark.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you want to turn left at an intersection on a green light but oncoming traffic is heavy, what should you do?
options: a:Use the next intersection instead.,b:Wait at the marked crosswalk for traffic to clear.,c:Enter the intersection and wait there for a safe gap before turning,d:Begin the turn and stop halfway
note: With a green light and heavy oncoming traffic, you may move into the intersection (without blocking the crosswalk) and wait with your wheels straight. When there is a safe gap or the light changes and oncoming traffic stops, complete your left turn.

question: When driving in fog, which lighting should you use?
options: a:Low beam headlights, and fog lights if equipped.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Parking lights only.
note: In fog, use low beam headlights because their light aims down at the road and reduces glare. If your vehicle has fog lights, use them with low beams. High beams reflect off the fog and can make it harder to see.

question: If you drink socially, what measure helps ensure a safe trip home?
options: a:Drink coffee before driving.,b:Ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.,c:Take a cold shower before driving.
note: Arrange a sober ride home, designate a driver, or use alternative transportation; coffee or showers do not sober you up.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a reduced conflict intersection, are left turns allowed?
options: a:True — left turns are allowed directly at the intersection.,b:False — direct left turns are not allowed; drivers use right turns and U‑turns instead.,c:Only if signed.,d:Only during daylight.
note: At reduced conflict intersections (often called J‑turn or RCUT intersections), drivers do not make direct left turns from the main road. Instead, they turn right and then make a U‑turn at a designated opening. Because left turns are specifically removed to reduce severe crashes, you should not expect to make a direct left turn at these intersections unless special signing clearly allows it.

question: How should drivers respond to a steady green arrow traffic signal?
options: a:Should slow to a stop, if it is safe to do so.,b:Should merge into a lane in the direction of the arrow.,c:May turn in the direction of the arrow after yielding to traffic and pedestrians already in the intersection.
note: A steady green arrow means you have a protected turn in the direction of the arrow. You may proceed to turn in that direction, but you must still yield to any pedestrians in the crosswalk and to vehicles already in the intersection. You do not need to stop if the way is clear, but you must complete the turn safely and under control.

question: Do pedestrians in crosswalks and at intersections always have the right-of-way?
options: a:True — they always have right-of-way.,b:False — not always, but pedestrians have right-of-way at intersections and crosswalks.,c:Only if the crosswalk is marked.,d:Only during daylight hours.
note: Pedestrians generally have the right‑of‑way when crossing in crosswalks and at intersections, whether the crosswalk is marked or unmarked. Drivers must yield to pedestrians who are lawfully in the crosswalk. However, pedestrians do not always have the right‑of‑way in every situation (for example, if they suddenly step into traffic against a signal), so drivers and pedestrians must both act carefully.

question: When approaching railroad tracks, what should drivers do?
options: a:Slow down, look, listen, and be prepared to stop.,b:Speed up to cross before a gate lowers.,c:Try to drive around a lowered gate.,d:Ignore the tracks unless there are lights.
note: When approaching railroad tracks, always slow down, look both ways, and listen for trains. Be prepared to stop if a train is approaching or if warning devices (lights, bells, or gates) are active. Never try to beat a train, never drive around lowered gates, and only cross the tracks when you are sure there is enough space to clear them completely.

question: When faced with an oncoming car to your left and a bicyclist to your right, what is the safest action?
options: a:Let the car pass and then pass the bike.,b:Pull onto the shoulder.,c:Split the difference between the hazards.
note: When you face an oncoming vehicle on your left and a bicyclist on your right, avoid trying to squeeze between them. Let the oncoming car pass first so you only have one hazard to manage at a time. Then, when the opposing lane is clear and you can give the bicyclist plenty of space, safely move over and pass the bicycle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you cross a single broken white or yellow line?
options: a:Only when turning left into a driveway.,b:When it is safe and does not interfere with traffic.,c:Never under any circumstance.,d:Only to pass a disabled vehicle.
note: A single broken white line separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction; you may cross it to change lanes when it is safe. A single broken yellow line separates traffic moving in opposite directions; you may cross it to pass when it is safe and legal. In both cases, you must be sure you will not interfere with other traffic.

question: If another driver is tailgating you, what is the best course of action?
options: a:Move to the right if there is an open lane.,b:If no right lane exists, wait until clear and then reduce speed slowly to encourage them to pass.,c:Never slow down abruptly.,d:All of the above.
note: When someone is following too closely, create space rather than reacting aggressively. If there is a right lane, move over and let them pass. If there is no right lane, wait for a safe opportunity and gradually reduce your speed so they can go around you. Never brake suddenly, because that can cause a rear‑end collision.

question: To avoid collisions with vehicles in your blind spot, you should:
options: a:Adjust your rearview mirrors every few minutes.,b:Quickly turn your head to check the blind spot before changing lanes.,c:Honk your horn right before turning or changing lanes.
note: Every vehicle has blind spots that mirrors cannot cover. Before changing lanes, quickly turn your head and glance over your shoulder in the direction you are moving to check these blind spots. Do not rely only on mirrors, and do not use your horn as a substitute for checking.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle, when should you return to your original lane?
options: a:When the entire passed vehicle is visible in your rearview mirror.,b:Immediately after passing, regardless of visibility.,c:Only at the next traffic signal.
note: After passing, you should not move back into the lane until you have enough space ahead of the vehicle you passed. A good rule is to wait until you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror; this indicates you have a safe following distance before returning to the lane.

question: Which statement about driving on wet roads is true?
options: a:As speed increases, tires become less effective and hydroplaning risk rises.,b:Water has no effect if you have high-quality tires.,c:Deep water is less hazardous than shallow water.,d:Driving faster improves traction.
note: On wet roads, as your speed increases, your tires have less time to squeeze water out from under the tread. This reduces traction and increases the risk of hydroplaning, where your tires ride on top of the water and lose contact with the road. Slowing down in wet conditions helps maintain control.

question: Which traffic light indicates you should slow and proceed with caution rather than stop?
options: a:Flashing yellow light.,b:Flashing red light.,c:Solid yellow light.,d:Solid red light.
note: A flashing yellow light means proceed with caution. You do not have to stop, but you should slow down, scan carefully for hazards such as cross traffic or pedestrians, and continue only when it is safe.

question: When traffic is merging near a construction zone using a zipper merge, what is the recommended driver behavior?
options: a:Stay in your lane until the point of merge, then take turns with other vehicles.,b:Merge into the adjacent lane as early as possible.,c:Change lanes immediately when you see a 'Lane closed ahead' sign.,d:Stop at the 'Lane closed ahead' sign and wait for traffic to clear.
note: In a zipper merge, drivers use both lanes fully up to the merge point, then take turns merging like the teeth of a zipper. Staying in your lane until the merge point and alternating with other vehicles keeps traffic flowing more smoothly and reduces backups near construction zones.

question: Which color lines divide lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions?
options: a:Yellow,b:White,c:Red
note: Yellow center lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. White lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction, and red is generally used for things like reflectors or curb markings, not for dividing opposing traffic lanes.

question: A downward-facing triangular sign generally means:
options: a:Indicate school zones.,b:Tells drivers to yield.,c:Indicate construction zones.
note: A downward-pointing triangle is the standard shape for a yield sign. When you see this sign, you must slow down, be prepared to stop, and yield the right-of-way to traffic and pedestrians already in or close to the intersection.

question: When parallel parking between two vehicles, what is the first step?
options: a:Turn your wheels to the left.,b:Pull up even with the car in front of your desired parking space.,c:Turn your wheels to the right.
note: To begin parallel parking, first pull up alongside and even with the vehicle in front of the space, leaving a safe gap. Then signal, check mirrors and blind spots, and start backing slowly while turning the wheel to enter the space.

question: Which statement best describes drivers who have consumed alcohol?
options: a:They are always aware of the risks.,b:They typically lack sufficient control over their bodies and judgment.,c:They become better drivers due to increased confidence.,d:They are more alert than sober drivers.
note: Alcohol slows reaction time and impairs judgment, coordination, and vision. Because of this, drivers who have been drinking usually do not have full control over their bodies or decisions, making driving unsafe.

question: What color are signs that indicate areas of public recreation or historical interest?
options: a:Red.,b:Orange.,c:Brown.,d:Green.
note: Brown traffic signs are used for recreational and cultural interest areas, such as parks, campgrounds, and historic sites. Recognizing brown signs helps you locate these public recreation or historical areas.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an officer is directing traffic at a working traffic light, what should drivers do?
options: a:Follow the officer's directions instead of the traffic light.,b:Follow the traffic light regardless of the officer.,c:Honk at the officer to confirm instructions.
note: When a police officer or authorized person is directing traffic, their hand signals and directions override traffic lights and signs. You must follow the officer’s instructions, even if the traffic signal shows a different indication.

question: Which of these is recommended for safer night driving?
options: a:Decrease your following distance.,b:Avoid driving only if you are tired.,c:Ensure your headlights are functioning properly.,d:Use high beams at all times.
note: At night, visibility is reduced, so it is important to make sure your headlights are clean, properly aimed, and working on both low and high beam. You should also increase your following distance and avoid driving when you are tired.

question: A red traffic signal requires you to:
options: a:Stop before entering any crosswalk.,b:Stop before entering the intersection.,c:Stop at the marked stop line or, if none, before the crosswalk or intersection.
note: A steady red traffic signal means you must come to a complete stop at the marked stop line. If there is no stop line, stop before entering the crosswalk. If there is no crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection. Always stop where you can see cross traffic but before you block any crosswalk or intersection.

question: What lane width is a motorcycle entitled to use on the roadway?
options: a:Half the lane width.,b:A marked bicycle lane only.,c:The same full lane width as other vehicles.,d:Only the right edge of a lane.
note: A motorcycle is entitled to use an entire traffic lane, just like a car. Other drivers should not crowd a motorcycle or share the lane side‑by‑side with it, because motorcycles need the full lane for safe maneuvering and to avoid road hazards.

question: When stopped at a railroad crossing with multiple tracks, when may you proceed?
options: a:As soon as the first train passes.,b:Wait until you have a clear view of all tracks before crossing.,c:Proceed if no gate is down.,d:Cross immediately if lights stop flashing.
note: At a crossing with more than one track, a second train can come from either direction, even right after the first one passes. You must wait until you can clearly see down all tracks in both directions and are sure no train is coming before you start across.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane, two-way road, you must:
options: a:Not cross the centerline.,b:Flash your lights at oncoming traffic.,c:Use the shoulder.,d:Only pass when you can safely use the lane for oncoming traffic to complete the pass.
note: On a two‑lane, two‑way road, you usually must move into the oncoming lane to pass. Only pass when the centerline allows it, you have enough clear distance to enter the oncoming lane, pass, and return to your lane safely without speeding or cutting off another vehicle.

question: Are blue, flashing, or strobe lights permitted on personal vehicles?
options: a:False — only authorized emergency or other specifically authorized vehicles may display blue, flashing, or strobe lights.,b:True
note: Blue, flashing, or strobe lights are reserved for authorized emergency and certain maintenance or service vehicles so other road users can quickly recognize them and yield. Personal vehicles may not display these lights because they can confuse other drivers and interfere with real emergency responses.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing without lights or gates, what should you do?
options: a:Cross the tracks immediately and as quickly as possible.,b:Always stop before crossing the tracks.,c:Prepare to yield to any train at the crossing.
note: At a crossing without lights or gates, you must approach with caution: slow down, look and listen carefully for trains in both directions, and be ready to stop. Cross only when you are sure no train is coming and never stop or shift gears while you are on the tracks.

question: When should you increase your following distance?
options: a:Following a motorcycle.,b:Exiting an expressway.,c:Driving behind a large vehicle that blocks your vision.,d:All of the above.
note: You should increase your following distance any time conditions make it harder to see, stop, or react in time. This includes when you are behind a large vehicle that blocks your view, when following motorcycles or bicycles (they can stop or fall quickly), in bad weather, heavy traffic, or when someone is tailgating you. More space gives you extra time to avoid sudden hazards.

question: Are drivers always required to stop for a stopped school bus on a two-lane road?
options: a:TRUE,b:FALSE
note: On a two-lane road, traffic in both directions must stop for a school bus when its red lights are flashing and the stop arm is extended. You must remain stopped until the lights stop flashing, the stop arm is withdrawn, and the bus starts moving again or the driver signals you to proceed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On which signal do you have the right-of-way to turn left?
options: a:Solid green circular light.,b:A flashing yellow arrow.,c:A green arrow pointing left.,d:A steady red light.
note: A green left-turn arrow is a protected turn signal: oncoming traffic and pedestrians facing you have a red light, so you have the right-of-way to turn left. A solid green circular light or flashing yellow arrow only allow a left turn if you yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians; they do not give you automatic right-of-way.

question: Orange-colored road signs usually indicate:
options: a:Regulatory signs.,b:Work zone signs.,c:School zone signs.
note: Orange road signs are used for temporary traffic control in work zones. They warn of construction, maintenance, or utility work and related hazards so you can slow down, be alert for workers and equipment, and follow any changed traffic patterns.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes on a highway, which steps should you take?
options: a:Signal, check mirrors, and check your blind spot by glancing over your shoulder.,b:Only signal; mirrors are optional.,c:Change lanes without signaling if traffic is light.
note: Before changing lanes, signal well in advance, check your mirrors to see traffic behind and beside you, then quickly glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Only move into the new lane when it is clear and safe. Signaling and checking both mirrors and blind spots are always required, even when traffic seems light.

question: You should leave a larger space cushion than usual when stopping:
options: a:On an incline.,b:At an intersection.,c:At a stop sign.,d:When parking.
note: When you stop on an uphill slope, the vehicle in front of you can roll backward when it starts to move. Leaving a larger space cushion gives you time and room to react so you can avoid being hit or having to back up into the car behind you.

question: You may not park within how many feet of a crosswalk at an intersection?
options: a:10 feet,b:20 feet,c:40 feet
note: Parking too close to a crosswalk blocks drivers’ and pedestrians’ view of each other. Staying at least 20 feet back from a crosswalk at an intersection helps everyone see and react in time, reducing the chance of a collision.

question: How does eating or drinking while driving affect driving?
options: a:It creates distractions that make vehicle control and lane keeping more difficult.,b:It makes drivers better because they are not hungry.,c:It results in no driving errors.
note: Eating or drinking while driving takes at least one hand off the wheel and your eyes and attention off the road. This makes it harder to steer smoothly, stay in your lane, and react quickly to hazards, increasing crash risk.

question: Are motorists required to yield to pedestrians who are walking against the traffic light?
options: a:True — motorists need not yield.,b:False — drivers must always yield to pedestrians.,c:Only if the pedestrian is in a marked crosswalk.,d:Only during daytime hours.
note: Drivers must always do everything possible to avoid hitting a pedestrian, even one crossing against the light. However, right‑of‑way laws generally require drivers to yield to pedestrians who are in a marked or unmarked crosswalk at an intersection. A pedestrian who walks against the traffic signal outside a crosswalk is not automatically given the legal right‑of‑way, but you must still slow, be prepared to stop, and avoid a collision.

question: How should drivers view railroad crossings?
options: a:Safe to cross, as it is unlikely that a train will be coming.,b:Dangerous.,c:Safe locations to park a car.
note: Trains are large, fast, and cannot stop quickly, so any railroad crossing must be treated as potentially dangerous. Always slow down, look and listen for trains, and obey warning signs, signals, and gates before crossing the tracks.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, into which lane should you complete your turn?
options: a:In the center of the street.,b:In the left lane of the one-way street.,c:In the right lane of the one-way street.,d:Into the bicycle lane.
note: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, you must turn into the nearest available lane going your direction. From the left lane of the two-way street, that is normally the left lane of the one-way street. This keeps your path short, avoids cutting across lanes, and reduces the chance of a collision with vehicles already on the one-way street.

question: At a school crossing sign, what should a driver do?
options: a:Watch for children and be prepared to stop.,b:Always stop whether there is a stop sign or not.,c:Always sound your horn when you see children.
note: A school crossing sign warns that children may be crossing the road. You must slow down, watch carefully for children, and be prepared to stop. Always yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk. You are not required to stop every time you see the sign unless there are children or a crossing guard indicating you must stop, or a stop sign or signal requires it.

question: If a tire blows out while driving, what is the best immediate action?
options: a:Gradually slow down and pull off the side of the road.,b:Do not immediately use your brakes.,c:Take your foot off the gas.,d:Hold the steering wheel firmly, ease off the gas, avoid hard braking, and steer to a safe place off the road.
note: If a tire blows out, hold the steering wheel firmly and keep the vehicle going straight. Ease your foot off the gas and let the car slow down gradually; avoid hard braking because it can cause you to lose control, especially with a flat tire. Once you have slowed and have control, carefully steer to the side of the road and stop in a safe place.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you reach an intersection and are not in the proper lane to turn, what should you do?
options: a:Drive to the next intersection and make the turn from the proper lane.,b:Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.,c:Turn on your blinker and make the turn from your current lane.
note: If you are not in the correct lane when you reach an intersection, you must go straight and continue to the next intersection, then get into the proper lane and make your turn there. Sudden lane changes or turning from the wrong lane can surprise other drivers and cause crashes.

question: What should you do when rain starts while you are driving?
options: a:Slow down and turn on headlights; if visibility is very poor, pull off and wait.,b:Drive at the maximum posted speed limit.,c:Drive faster than surrounding traffic to get through quickly.
note: When rain begins, roads are especially slippery because oil and dirt mix with the water. You should slow down, increase your following distance, and turn on your headlights so you can see and be seen. If the rain is so heavy that you cannot see well, safely pull off the road, turn on your hazard lights, and wait until conditions improve.

question: If your accelerator becomes stuck while driving, what is the immediate correct response?
options: a:Reach down to free the pedal with your hand.,b:Shift into park and then call for help.,c:Shift to neutral, apply steady braking, and pull off the road when safe.,d:Turn off the ignition while still moving.
note: If the accelerator sticks, keep your eyes on the road, shift to neutral, and apply firm, steady braking. Steer smoothly to the side of the road and stop in a safe place. Once stopped, turn off the engine and call for assistance. Do not reach down to free the pedal or turn off the ignition while moving, as you can lose steering and control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following actions should you take when preparing to make a left turn?
options: a:Signal, check for oncoming vehicles and pedestrians, and yield as needed.,b:Signal and immediately increase speed.,c:Signal only if there is visible traffic.,d:Signal and move into the right lane before turning.
note: Before a left turn, signal well in advance, move into the correct lane, and slow as needed. Check for oncoming traffic, bicyclists, and pedestrians in the crosswalk. You must yield to oncoming vehicles going straight or turning right and to pedestrians crossing your path before completing the turn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a steady green traffic light allow you to do?
options: a:You must slow down and prepare to stop.,b:You may drive through the intersection if the road is clear.,c:You must stop and check for oncoming traffic before proceeding.,d:You may only turn right on green.
note: A steady green light means you may go straight or turn if it is safe, but it does not give you the right to ignore other road users. You must yield to pedestrians in crosswalks and to oncoming traffic when turning left. Always enter the intersection at a safe speed and be prepared for vehicles that may still be clearing the intersection.

question: If you stop on the roadside at night, which lighting should you use?
options: a:Turn on your emergency flashers and use low beam headlights only if they will not blind oncoming traffic.,b:Turn off all your lights.,c:Use only your parking lights.
note: If you must stop on the roadside at night, you want other drivers to see you clearly. Turn on your emergency flashers so your vehicle is more noticeable, and use your low beam headlights if they will not shine directly into oncoming traffic. In many situations, especially on narrow or two‑lane roads, it is safer to rely on hazard flashers and parking lights so you are visible without creating glare for approaching drivers.

question: If the driver ahead appears distracted (one hand on the wheel, talking to a passenger), you should:
options: a:Give the vehicle extra space.,b:Know they are reducing their safety margin.,c:Avoid following them or copying their behavior.,d:All of the above
note: A distracted driver is more likely to make sudden or unsafe moves. Increase your following distance to give yourself more time to react, recognize that their reduced attention lowers their safety margin, and never copy their behavior. Staying alert and keeping extra space helps you avoid being involved in their potential mistakes.

question: If you encounter an animal on the roadway, how should you respond?
options: a:Exercise extreme caution and pass slowly to avoid startling it.,b:No special action is required.,c:Pass the animal as closely as possible.
note: When you see an animal on or near the road, slow down, be prepared to stop, and pass very cautiously. Sudden movements or loud engine noise can startle animals and cause them to run into your path, so give them extra space and time.

question: Drivers must yield to pedestrians under what circumstances?
options: a:Only when the pedestrian is in a crosswalk.,b:Only if the pedestrian is on the same side of the road as the driver.,c:Even if the pedestrian crosses carelessly.
note: Drivers must be prepared to yield to pedestrians in the roadway, even if the pedestrian is crossing carelessly or outside a crosswalk. You must do whatever is necessary to avoid hitting a pedestrian, because people on foot are much more vulnerable in a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it legal to pass another vehicle on the right?
options: a:On a narrow bridge.,b:If the vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is an available passing lane.,c:Even if it means driving off the pavement.
note: You may pass on the right only when it can be done safely and without leaving the paved roadway, such as when the vehicle ahead is turning left and there is a marked lane or enough legal space to pass, or on roads with two or more lanes going in your direction. Never pass on the right by driving off the pavement or onto the shoulder.

question: Why should car drivers be especially cautious around large trucks?
options: a:They have large blind spots and need more room to maneuver and stop.,b:They can stop more quickly than passenger vehicles.,c:They never need extra room to maneuver.,d:They are always easier to pass than cars.
note: Large trucks have big blind spots along the sides, behind, and sometimes directly in front of the cab, and they need much more distance to turn, change lanes, and stop. Give trucks extra space, avoid lingering beside them, and do not cut in front of them because they cannot stop as quickly as a car.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Lane-use control signals showing a green arrow tell drivers:
options: a:Drivers should not drive in this lane.,b:The signal is about to change to a red X.,c:Drivers may use this lane because it is open.
note: A green arrow over a lane means that lane is open for travel in the direction of the arrow. You may drive in that lane, but still must obey speed limits, signs, and any other markings that apply to that lane.

question: Is it legal to pass a school bus that is stopped with its red lights flashing?
options: a:True,b:False
note: When a school bus has its red lights flashing and the stop arm extended, you must stop and remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn. Passing the bus in this situation is illegal. On a divided highway with a physical median, drivers traveling in the opposite direction usually do not have to stop, but they still must use caution.

question: If someone is driving aggressively behind you, what should you do?
options: a:Make every effort to get out of their way.,b:Stare at the driver as they pass.,c:Speed up to prevent them passing you.,d:Brake-check them to slow them down.
note: If someone is driving aggressively behind you, stay calm and make every safe effort to get out of their way. Move to another lane or safely pull over if needed, and avoid eye contact or gestures that could escalate the situation. Never speed up, brake-check, or confront the aggressive driver.

question: What does a yellow and black diamond-shaped sign indicate?
options: a:A warning about conditions on or near the road ahead.,b:Directions to cities and towns.,c:Traffic laws and regulations.
note: Yellow and black diamond-shaped signs are warning signs. They alert you to special conditions or hazards ahead, such as curves, intersections, pedestrian crossings, or changes in road width, so you can slow down and proceed with caution.

question: What does an arrow painted on the pavement signify for drivers in that lane?
options: a:Drivers may choose to make the movement indicated by the arrow.,b:Drivers in that lane must make the movement indicated by the arrow.,c:Drivers must always stop before following the arrow.,d:Arrows apply only when traffic lights are out of service.
note: Lane-use arrows painted on the pavement tell you what movement is required from that lane, such as turn left, turn right, or go straight. When you are in a lane marked with a single arrow, you must make the movement shown, unless traffic signals or signs specifically allow another movement.

question: Which is true about emergency vehicles?
options: a:Have the right-of-way when using sirens, horns, and/or flashing lights.,b:May follow each other.,c:May use a loudspeaker to give instructions.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches using a siren and/or flashing red or blue lights, you must immediately yield the right-of-way by pulling to the right side of the road and stopping, when safe. Stay stopped until the vehicle has passed. Emergency vehicles may also use loudspeakers to give instructions and may travel in groups, so check for more than one before re-entering traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a right turn, where should your vehicle be positioned?
options: a:As close as possible to the right side of the road.,b:Near the center of the street.,c:Close to the left side of the street.
note: For a right turn, you should be in the lane closest to the right curb or edge of the roadway. This shortens your turn, keeps you predictable to other drivers, and reduces the chance of cutting across other lanes.

question: If the driver behind you wants to pass, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up.,b:Maintain your speed.,c:Slow down slightly if needed to allow room in front so the driver can pass safely.
note: If another driver wants to pass you, do not speed up or try to block them. Maintain a steady speed or slow slightly to create more space in front of you so the passing driver can move back into the lane safely. This reduces the risk of side‑by‑side conflicts and rear‑end collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a roadway from a private road or driveway, what should you do?
options: a:Blow your horn to warn cars you are entering the roadway.,b:Yield to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway.,c:Drive out fast to merge smoothly with the traffic.
note: When entering a roadway from a driveway or private road, you must yield to all pedestrians and vehicles already on the road. Wait until traffic is clear and you can enter without forcing other road users to slow or change lanes suddenly.

question: If your wheels drop off the pavement onto a shoulder, how should you return to the roadway?
options: a:Brake hard and sharply steer back onto the pavement.,b:Stop on the shoulder and re-enter when safe.,c:Slow down without braking sharply and carefully steer back onto the pavement.,d:Accelerate and swerve back onto the road.
note: If your wheels drop off the pavement, stay calm, ease off the accelerator, and avoid hard braking. When your speed is under control and traffic allows, gently steer back onto the pavement. Sudden braking or sharp swerving can cause you to lose control or skid.

question: How do you check your blind spot before changing lanes?
options: a:Look into the left or right side mirror only.,b:Look over your shoulder toward the direction you plan to move to check the blind spot.,c:Check only the rearview mirror.,d:Honk to alert other drivers instead of checking.
note: Mirrors do not show everything around your vehicle; there are areas called blind spots. Before changing lanes, quickly look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move to check these blind spots, then make your lane change if it is clear.

question: What does a regulatory sign with a red circle and slash over a black symbol indicate?
options: a:That drivers must stop.,b:That the indicated action is forbidden.,c:That some drivers must yield.,d:That parking is allowed at certain times.
note: A red circle with a diagonal slash over a black symbol is a regulatory "prohibition" sign. It means the action shown by the symbol (such as U-turn, right turn, or parking) is not allowed by law at that location.

question: 'Highway hypnosis' can result from what driving behavior?
options: a:Frequent rest stops.,b:Staring at the roadway for long periods of time.,c:Too much sleep the night before your trip.
note: Highway hypnosis is a trance-like state that can occur when you stare straight ahead at the road for long periods without moving your eyes. Your mind drifts, and you may not notice traffic or hazards. To prevent this, keep your eyes moving, scan mirrors and the road, and take regular breaks.

question: How often should you stop to relieve fatigue on a long trip?
options: a:Every two hours for a short break.,b:Do arm exercises every hour.,c:Drive with one eye open at a time.
note: On long trips, you should stop about every two hours for a short break to rest, stretch, and refresh. Regular breaks help prevent fatigue, which slows your reactions and makes it harder to pay attention to the road.

question: What is the first control you should adjust, if needed, when you get into a car to drive?
options: a:Your rearview mirror.,b:Your seat so you can see the road clearly.,c:The steering wheel.,d:Your radio.
note: When you get into the driver’s seat, adjust your seat first so you can reach the pedals and controls comfortably and see the road clearly. After the seat is set, adjust your mirrors and steering wheel to match your driving position.

question: As alcohol builds up in your system, what happens?
options: a:Makes you feel less confident.,b:Slows down your reactions.,c:Begins to metabolize itself more quickly.
note: As alcohol builds up in your system, it slows your reaction time, reduces coordination, and impairs judgment. Even small amounts can affect your ability to respond quickly to traffic situations, making driving unsafe.

question: Which best defines defensive driving?
options: a:Following the vehicle ahead at a close distance.,b:Identifying dangerous driving situations and taking action to avoid accidents.,c:Defending yourself against poor drivers by rushing ahead in traffic.
note: Defensive driving means constantly scanning the road, spotting potential hazards early, and adjusting your speed or position to prevent collisions. It is about anticipating what other drivers, pedestrians, or road conditions might do and acting early to stay safe.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?
options: a:Proceed with caution.,b:Merging traffic.,c:Pedestrian crossing.
note: A flashing yellow light does not require you to stop, but it does require extra caution. You should slow down, check for cross traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when it is safe to do so.

question: The statement 'The best way to avoid loss of control under wet conditions is to increase your vehicle's speed' is:
options: a:False,b:True
note: On wet roads, higher speeds increase the chance of hydroplaning, where your tires ride on a thin layer of water and lose contact with the road. To maintain control, you should slow down, avoid sudden steering or braking, and drive smoothly.

question: If a railroad crossing lacks active warning devices, you should slow down, look, and listen.
options: a:False,b:True
note: At railroad crossings without lights or gates, you must approach carefully, slow down, and look and listen for trains in both directions. Only cross the tracks when you are sure no train is coming and there is enough space to clear the tracks completely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it illegal to drive below the posted speed limit?
options: a:When in heavy traffic in a construction zone,b:Only when driving in rural areas,c:When driving slowly disrupts the normal flow of traffic.
note: Driving much slower than the normal flow of traffic can be dangerous because it forces other drivers to brake or change lanes suddenly. If you must drive slowly, stay in the right lane when possible, and do not drive so slowly that you unnecessarily block or disrupt traffic.

question: Is it safe to stop on railroad tracks even for a short time when moving with a line of vehicles?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Never stop on railroad tracks, even briefly. Before you cross, make sure there is enough space on the far side of the tracks for your entire vehicle so you do not get trapped if traffic stops.

question: What color is most commonly used for warning signs?
options: a:Yellow,b:Red,c:Green
note: Most general warning signs in the U.S. are diamond-shaped with a yellow background and black symbols or wording. They alert drivers to conditions such as curves, intersections, or pedestrian crossings ahead.

question: Which location is unlawful for parking?
options: a:In a parking lot.,b:On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.,c:On a hill.
note: Parking on a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane is illegal because it blocks pedestrians and cyclists and creates safety hazards. Always park only where it is permitted and within the required distance from the curb.

question: Which statement about seat belts and child restraints is accurate?
options: a:You should never place a rear-facing infant or small child in the front seat of a vehicle with a passenger airbag.,b:An airbag can be dangerous to an infant or small child, even in a low-speed collision.,c:You should always make sure all your passengers are using a seat belt or child restraint.,d:All of the above
note: Seat belts and proper child restraints greatly reduce injury risk. Children 12 and under are safest in the rear seat, properly restrained. Never place a rear‑facing infant seat in front of an active passenger airbag, because the airbag can seriously injure or kill a child even in a low‑speed crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering and driving in a roundabout, what should you do?
options: a:Stop inside the roundabout.,b:Yield to traffic already in the roundabout.,c:Drive clockwise around the central island.
note: When approaching a roundabout, slow down and yield to traffic already circulating within it, as well as to pedestrians in crosswalks. Enter when it is safe and travel counterclockwise around the central island until you reach your exit.

question: How can you help prevent rear-end collisions?
options: a:Release the gas pedal and let your vehicle slow before applying the brakes.,b:Before stopping, check your mirrors and blind spots for traffic.,c:Avoid sudden stops.
note: Rear-end collisions are often caused by sudden, unexpected stops. To reduce this risk, look ahead, slow down gradually by easing off the accelerator, and brake smoothly so drivers behind you have time to react. Checking your mirrors helps you stay aware of traffic behind, but the key preventive action is to avoid sudden stops.

question: As a pedestrian, what should you do when vehicles are approaching?
options: a:Always insist that vehicles stop for you in a crosswalk.,b:Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching.,c:Enter a crosswalk at any time because drivers must stop.,d:Assume vehicles will always stop for you.
note: Even when you have the right-of-way in a crosswalk, you must not step into the street in front of approaching vehicles that are too close to stop safely. Always wait until it is clearly safe, make sure drivers see you, and then cross; never assume vehicles will stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Does 'yield' sometimes mean you must stop if you cannot merge safely into traffic?
options: a:True,b:False
note: A yield sign means you must slow down and be prepared to stop. If other traffic has the right-of-way and you cannot merge or enter safely, you must stop and wait until there is a safe gap before proceeding.

question: If your tire blows out while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Slam on your brakes.,b:Hold the steering wheel firmly, reduce speed, and pull to a safe stop.,c:Keep driving normally.
note: When a tire blows out, the sudden loss of air can pull your vehicle to one side. Hold the steering wheel firmly, stay off the brakes at first, ease off the accelerator to slow down, then gently steer to a safe place off the road and stop once you are under control.

question: How does being distracted affect a driver's reaction to hazards?
options: a:It usually causes slower reactions to hazards.,b:It never causes danger.,c:It causes drivers to drive faster.
note: Distractions such as phones, passengers, or adjusting controls take your attention away from the road. This usually slows your reaction time to hazards, making it harder to notice and respond in time and increasing your risk of a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a posted speed limit represent?
options: a:The exact speed at which you must travel to avoid a ticket.,b:The maximum legal driving speed under ideal road and weather conditions.,c:Only a recommended driving speed.
note: A posted speed limit is the maximum legal speed allowed on that road in ideal conditions, not a required speed. You must often drive slower than the limit when conditions are poor (rain, fog, heavy traffic, sharp curves) so that you can stop safely and maintain control of your vehicle.

question: When near a blind pedestrian using a cane or guide dog, how should you drive?
options: a:Slow down, be prepared to stop, and yield the right-of-way.,b:Take the right-of-way.,c:Proceed normally.
note: When a pedestrian is blind or visually impaired and using a white cane or guide dog, you must yield the right-of-way. Slow down well in advance, be prepared to stop, and never honk or rev your engine, as this can confuse or frighten the person. Wait until they are safely out of your path before proceeding.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a traffic light changes from green to yellow as you approach an intersection, what is the appropriate response?
options: a:Be prepared to stop safely because the light will soon turn red.,b:Accelerate to beat the red light.,c:Stop abruptly in the middle of the intersection.,d:Ignore it and proceed at the same speed.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. If you can stop safely before the intersection, you should slow down and stop. If you are too close to stop safely when it turns yellow, continue through with caution rather than braking abruptly and risking a rear-end collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it permissible to pass when there is a solid yellow line on your side of the centerline?
options: a:Yes — you may pass anytime.,b:No — you may not pass when a solid yellow line is on your side.,c:Only if the other car signals.,d:Only at night.
note: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means you must not cross it to pass another vehicle. Passing is only allowed where the line on your side is broken, because that indicates you have enough visibility and it is legal to move into the opposing lane when it is safe.

question: What does a green arrow displayed for a traffic lane indicate?
options: a:It applies only on one-way streets.,b:Traffic in the indicated lane is permitted to move only in the arrow's direction and is given a protected movement for that direction.,c:You may proceed only if there is also a circular green light.,d:The lane is closing soon.
note: A green arrow means you are permitted to move only in the direction the arrow points, and you have the right-of-way for that specific movement after yielding to any vehicles or pedestrians already in the intersection. It does not require a circular green light and does not apply only to one-way streets.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should drivers respond to a steady red traffic light?
options: a:Proceed if there is no crossing traffic.,b:Stop completely; a right turn on red is allowed unless prohibited.,c:Slow and continue through the intersection.,d:Turn left without yielding.
note: A steady red means stop. You may turn right on red after coming to a complete stop unless a sign prohibits it and if the way is clear.

question: You may pass another vehicle if the dividing line between lanes is what type?
options: a:Broken white.,b:Solid yellow.,c:Double solid yellow.
note: A broken white line separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. You may cross a broken white line to change lanes or pass when it is safe. Solid yellow or double solid yellow lines generally mean passing is not allowed or is restricted.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing with signals flashing, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down and look for a train.,b:Stop and look for a train.,c:Look for a train, then speed up.
note: When the lights are flashing or gates are down at a railroad crossing, you must stop and not proceed until the signals stop, the gates are fully raised, and you are sure no train is coming. Stop at least 15 feet from the nearest rail and never try to go around lowered gates.

question: How should you prepare for hazards coming up on the road ahead?
options: a:Stare straight ahead at all times.,b:Continually scan the entire road and all roadsides.,c:Drive with your left foot resting lightly on the brake pedal.
note: To prepare for hazards, keep your eyes moving and scan the road ahead, to the sides, and behind you. This helps you spot problems early, such as slowing traffic, pedestrians, or obstacles, so you have more time to react safely.

question: If you become stranded in a snowstorm, what should you do?
options: a:Lay down in your car and go to sleep.,b:Stay in your car and wait for help.,c:Get out of the car and go for help.,d:Walk into the road to get the attention of other drivers.
note: If you are stranded in a snowstorm, it is usually safest to stay in your vehicle. Your car provides shelter and makes it easier for rescuers to find you. Run the engine only occasionally for heat, keep a window slightly open for fresh air, and make your vehicle visible with lights or markers.

question: How can you avoid staying in a truck or bus blind spot?
options: a:Never pass large vehicles under any circumstances.,b:Avoid driving alongside them and do not tailgate.,c:Flash your lights to alert them of your presence.,d:Follow directly behind them.
note: Large trucks and buses have large blind spots along both sides and directly behind them. To stay out of these no‑zones, avoid driving alongside them for long periods and never follow too closely. Pass promptly and safely, and leave extra space so the driver can see you in their mirrors.

question: Is it acceptable to drive around lowered railroad crossing gates?
options: a:When the lights have stopped flashing.,b:Under no circumstances.,c:When the train has passed.
note: It is illegal and extremely dangerous to drive around lowered railroad crossing gates. A second train may be coming, or the train may be closer or faster than it appears. You must wait until the gates are fully raised, the lights stop flashing, and it is clearly safe before crossing.

question: For persons age 21 or older, what minimum BAC is illegal for driving in Minnesota?
options: a:0.05 percent.,b:0.08 percent.,c:0.02 percent.,d:0.10 percent.
note: It is illegal for drivers age 21 and older to operate a motor vehicle with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher.

question: If a fire engine is following you but is not using its emergency signals, how should you respond?
options: a:Continue to drive in a normal manner.,b:Stop as quickly as you can.,c:Speed up to get out of its way.,d:Pull to the side and stop.
note: You are required to yield and pull to the right and stop only when an emergency vehicle is using its lights and/or siren. If a fire engine is behind you without any emergency signals activated, treat it like any other vehicle and continue driving normally while obeying all traffic laws.

question: An eight-sided (octagonal) sign always means:
options: a:Hospital sign.,b:Stop sign.,c:Speed limit sign.
note: An eight‑sided (octagonal) sign is reserved exclusively for STOP signs. When you see this shape, you must come to a complete stop at the stop line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection, then proceed only when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is passing prohibited?
options: a:On a hill or curve, approaching an intersection, or when a school bus's lights are flashing.,b:Only at night.,c:When the car ahead is driving below the speed limit.,d:Across a broken centerline.
note: Passing is unsafe and usually illegal when you cannot clearly see oncoming traffic, such as on hills or curves, when you are near intersections or railroad crossings, or when a stopped school bus has its red lights flashing and stop arm extended. In these situations you must stay behind and wait until it is clearly safe and legal to pass.

question: At a crossing with only a crossbuck (no gate or lights), what should you do?
options: a:Only continue once cleared to do so by a flagger.,b:Turn your radio down to hear if a train may be approaching.,c:Approach with caution, look and listen for trains, and cross only when the tracks are clear in both directions.
note: A crossbuck alone means you are at a railroad crossing but there are no gates or flashing lights to warn you of trains. You must slow down, look and listen carefully in both directions, and only cross the tracks when you are sure no train is coming and there is enough space to clear the tracks completely.

question: A solid white edge line that slants left indicates:
options: a:There is an intersection just ahead.,b:The road will become narrower ahead.,c:You will be required to turn left just ahead.
note: A solid white edge line marks the outer edge of the roadway. When that right edge line angles or slants toward the center of the road, it is warning you that the usable roadway is narrowing ahead, so you should be prepared to adjust your position and speed.

question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, what should you do?
options: a:Try to get even with the aggressive driver.,b:Stay calm and move out of the aggressive driver's way.,c:Call the police immediately.
note: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, focus on safety, not on being right. Stay calm, avoid eye contact or gestures, and safely slow down or change lanes to give them space. Do not try to block, chase, or confront them, because escalating the situation greatly increases the risk of a crash.

question: When interacting with pedestrians, what is the driver's responsibility?
options: a:Ensure the pedestrian is aware of your vehicle.,b:Always yield the right-of-way even if the pedestrian is wrong.,c:Yield the right-of-way only when the pedestrian has legal right-of-way.,d:Stop only if the pedestrian is in a marked crosswalk.
note: Drivers must use extra care around pedestrians because they are unprotected and easily injured. Even if a pedestrian is crossing illegally, you must do everything you reasonably can to avoid hitting them, including slowing or stopping. You should always be prepared to yield whenever necessary to prevent a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When driving with other traffic, what is the safest speed approach?
options: a:Drive with the flow of traffic within the posted limit.,b:Fluctuate your speed to stay alert.,c:Drive slower than the flow of traffic.
note: Driving at a speed that matches the flow of traffic, while staying within the posted speed limit, is generally safest. Moving much faster or much slower than surrounding traffic increases the chance of conflicts, sudden lane changes, and rear-end collisions.

question: To reduce the effects of headlight glare from oncoming vehicles at night, where should you look?
options: a:Look over your shoulder.,b:Keep your eyes on the right side of the road ahead.,c:At the center of the road ahead.
note: At night, bright oncoming headlights can temporarily blind you. To reduce glare, look toward the right edge of your lane and use the white line or road edge as a guide until the vehicle passes, while still checking the road ahead with quick glances.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a freeway, what is usually best?
options: a:Proceed slowly while waiting for an opening.,b:Accelerate to the speed of freeway traffic and merge smoothly.,c:Turn on your hazard lights until safely on the freeway.
note: On a freeway on‑ramp, use the acceleration lane to reach a speed close to that of freeway traffic, signal, and merge smoothly when there is a safe gap. Entering traffic must yield to vehicles already on the freeway.

question: Before starting the ignition, what safety check should you complete regarding seat belts?
options: a:Buckle only backseat passengers.,b:Make sure all passengers who require belts are buckled, including yourself.,c:Buckle only child passengers.,d:Wait until after starting the car to buckle up.
note: Before starting the vehicle, buckle your own seat belt and make sure every passenger who is required to use a seat belt is properly buckled. Making this a habit greatly reduces the risk of serious injury in a crash.

question: If you leave your vehicle unattended, what must you do?
options: a:Turn off the engine.,b:Lock the ignition and remove the key.,c:Set the parking brake.
note: When leaving a vehicle unattended, you must stop the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.

question: A red flashing traffic light has the same meaning as a:
options: a:Solid red light,b:Stop sign,c:Yield sign,d:No parking sign
note: A flashing red light means you must treat the intersection like a stop sign: come to a complete stop, check for traffic and pedestrians in all directions, and proceed only when it is safe.

question: Your blind spot is the area of the road:
options: a:You see in your rearview mirror.,b:You cannot see without moving your head.,c:Directly behind your vehicle.
note: Blind spots are areas around your vehicle that you cannot see using your mirrors alone. To check them, you must briefly turn your head and look over your shoulder before changing lanes or merging.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a steady green arrow shown with a red light allow you to do?
options: a:You may drive only in the direction of the green arrow.,b:You must wait for a solid green light to proceed in any direction.,c:You may only drive straight ahead.
note: A steady green arrow means you have a protected turn in the direction of the arrow, even if the other signals are red. You may proceed only in that direction, and only after making sure the intersection is clear of pedestrians and other traffic.

question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, what must you do?
options: a:Assume the flagger is not supposed to be directing traffic.,b:Copy what surrounding traffic is doing despite the flagger's instructions.,c:Follow the directions given by the flagger.
note: In construction zones, flaggers have the same authority as traffic signals or signs. You must follow their instructions, slow down, and proceed carefully to protect workers and other road users.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching an uncontrolled intersection, what is the safe action a driver should take?
options: a:Stop and check in all directions before proceeding.,b:Maintain your speed and proceed through.,c:Yield to vehicles approaching from the right and be prepared to stop.,d:Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection, you must be ready to yield, especially to vehicles approaching from your right. Slow down, cover the brake, and look left, right, and left again so you can stop if another driver enters the intersection.

question: How should a lap belt be positioned to be effective?
options: a:Loose across the waist,b:Buckled snugly low across your hip bones and upper thighs,c:Hidden beneath the seat,d:High across the stomach
note: A lap belt should be worn low and snug across the hip bones and upper thighs, not across the soft part of the stomach. This helps the strong pelvic bones absorb crash forces and reduces the risk of internal injuries. The shoulder belt should cross the middle of the chest and shoulder, not under the arm or behind the back, and should fit snugly without slack.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, which vehicle should yield?
options: a:The vehicle on the right has the right-of-way; the vehicle on the left must yield.,b:Drivers should make hand motions to decide who goes.,c:The vehicle on the left has the right-of-way.,d:Whoever honks first has the right-of-way.
note: At a four-way stop, drivers proceed in the order they arrive. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. Clear right-of-way rules help prevent confusion and collisions at intersections.

question: If there are two parallel railroad tracks, what should you do after one train passes?
options: a:When one train passes, look for another train on the other track before proceeding.,b:It is always safe to proceed after one train passes.,c:You must always stop before crossing the tracks.
note: When there are multiple tracks, one train passing can hide another train coming from either direction on the other track. After the first train passes, wait until you can clearly see down all tracks in both directions and are sure no other train is approaching before you proceed.

question: How can stress affect your driving?
options: a:Lowering your ability to focus on driving.,b:Decreasing your chances of an accident.,c:Making you more alert and improving your driving.
note: Stress and strong emotions can distract you, narrow your attention, and lead to poor decisions or aggressive driving. This lowers your ability to focus on traffic, signs, and hazards, increasing your risk of a crash. If you are very upset or angry, it is safer to delay driving until you have calmed down.

question: If your vehicle does not have ABS and you must stop quickly, what should you do?
options: a:Lightly tap the brakes repeatedly.,b:Firmly pump the brakes until the vehicle stops.,c:Hold the brake pedal down continuously without pumping.,d:Shift into neutral and coast to a stop.
note: In a vehicle without ABS, use the "pump" or threshold braking method in an emergency stop: apply firm pressure to the brake pedal, release slightly before the wheels lock, then reapply. This pumping action helps you slow quickly while still being able to steer and avoid skidding.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your freeway exit, what should you do?
options: a:Go to the next exit.,b:Make a U-turn across the median.,c:Pull onto the shoulder and back up to the exit.,d:Stop and wait for traffic to clear then reverse.
note: If you miss your exit, stay calm and keep going to the next one. Never stop on the freeway, back up, or make a U-turn across the median, because these actions are extremely dangerous and illegal. Exit safely at the next opportunity and then re-route to your destination.

question: What should you do when driving in foggy conditions?
options: a:Turn on your hazard lights.,b:Turn on your low beam headlights.,c:It is okay to drive at the maximum speed limit.
note: In fog, always use low-beam headlights because their light aims down at the road and reduces glare. High beams reflect off the water droplets in fog and can make it harder to see. Slow down and increase following distance whenever visibility is reduced.

question: If your wheels slip off the edge of the road, what is the recommended action?
options: a:Slow down gradually, then steer back onto the pavement when safe.,b:Jerk the steering wheel to force the vehicle back onto the pavement.,c:Slam on your brakes and stop.
note: If your wheels drop off the pavement, keep a firm grip on the wheel, ease off the accelerator, and slow down gradually. Do not jerk the steering wheel or slam on the brakes, as this can cause you to lose control. When the car is under control and your speed is reduced, gently steer back onto the pavement when it is safe.

question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, how must you respond?
options: a:Follow the crossing guard's directions.,b:Follow what nearby cars are doing instead.,c:Ignore the crossing guard if signs differ.,d:Speed through the zone to clear it quickly.
note: When a crossing guard is present, their directions override signs and signals for traffic in that area. You must follow the crossing guard’s instructions and drive slowly and carefully, watching for children and pedestrians in the school zone.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two drivers arrive simultaneously at an open intersection, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on the right has the right-of-way.,b:The driver on the left has the right-of-way.,c:Either driver may proceed without stopping.,d:The faster vehicle has the right-of-way.
note: At an uncontrolled or open intersection where two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the right has the right-of-way. The driver on the left must yield. If there is any doubt, both drivers should communicate with signals and proceed cautiously.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you always use your turn signal?
options: a:Changing lanes, pulling into or out of a parking space, or entering traffic from an alley.,b:Only when turning right.,c:Only when other vehicles are present.,d:Only at night.
note: You must always signal before any change in direction or position that could affect other road users, including changing lanes, pulling into or out of a parking space, and entering traffic from an alley or driveway. Signaling lets others know your intentions so they can react safely.

question: What sequence of checks should you perform just before changing lanes?
options: a:Quickly turn your head and change lanes immediately.,b:Check side view mirror, rearview mirror, and glance over your shoulder for blind spots.,c:Only check the rearview mirror.,d:Honk to alert other drivers then move.
note: Before changing lanes, first check your mirrors to see traffic behind and beside you, then quickly glance over your shoulder in the direction you’re moving to check your blind spot. Only change lanes when it is clear and safe to do so.

question: If your vehicle is blocking traffic after an accident, what should you do if possible?
options: a:Move the vehicle off the traveled portion of the roadway.,b:Never move the vehicle under any circumstances.,c:Wait for police before attempting to move the vehicle.,d:Abandon the vehicle and leave the scene.
note: After a minor crash, if there are no serious injuries and the vehicles are drivable, you should move your vehicle out of the traffic lane to the shoulder or a safe area. This reduces the risk of another collision and keeps traffic flowing, as long as it is safe to move the vehicle.

question: Regulatory signs are usually which color and must always be obeyed?
options: a:Blue.,b:Green.,c:White.,d:Yellow.
note: Regulatory signs tell you what you must do or must not do, such as speed limits, no parking, or one-way directions. They are commonly white with black or red lettering or symbols, and drivers are legally required to obey them.

question: Is it lawful for a car to try to share a single lane with a motorcycle?
options: a:TRUE,b:FALSE
note: A motorcycle is entitled to use the full width of a traffic lane, just like a car. Other vehicles must not crowd or share the same lane side‑by‑side with a motorcycle because it reduces the rider’s space to maneuver and creates a serious safety hazard.

question: Which statement about alcohol's effects is correct?
options: a:Alcohol does not limit concentration, perception, judgment, and memory.,b:Only a blood alcohol level greater than the legal limit can limit concentration.,c:Even the smallest amount of alcohol can limit concentration, perception, judgment, and memory.
note: Even small amounts of alcohol affect the brain and can reduce concentration, slow perception, and impair judgment and memory. Because driving requires constant attention and quick decisions, any amount of alcohol can negatively affect driving ability, even if you are below the legal limit.

question: When passing a large vehicle, what should the driver of a small vehicle expect?
options: a:Loud noises only.,b:Increased wind gusts that can affect steering.,c:No change in driving conditions.,d:Guaranteed slower travel behind the vehicle.
note: Large trucks and buses push a lot of air around them. As you pass, you may feel a strong wind gust that can pull or push your smaller vehicle sideways. Hold the steering wheel firmly and be prepared to make small corrections while passing and when you move back in front of the large vehicle.

question: Before driving an unfamiliar vehicle you are borrowing, what should you do?
options: a:Drive immediately without checking the controls.,b:Hide from your friend that you are unfamiliar with the vehicle.,c:Take a few minutes to locate and test essential controls and correct any defects.
note: Before driving any unfamiliar vehicle, take a few minutes to adjust the seat and mirrors and locate and test essential controls such as the turn signals, headlights, wipers, brakes, gear selector, and horn. Do not drive the vehicle if you notice any safety-related defects until they are corrected.

question: When should you return to your previous lane after passing another vehicle?
options: a:When you sense that you are far enough ahead of the other vehicle.,b:When the other vehicle signals for you to return to the lane.,c:When you can see the entire passed vehicle in your rearview mirror (or its headlights).
note: After passing, do not move back into the lane until you can see the entire front of the vehicle you passed (or both of its headlights at night) in your rearview mirror. This ensures you have enough space and reduces the risk of cutting the other driver off. Always signal before returning to your lane.

question: Why must you use extra caution near a pedestrian carrying a white cane?
options: a:He or she is a police officer.,b:He or she is deaf.,c:He or she is blind.
note: A white cane (with or without a red tip) or a guide dog identifies a blind or visually impaired pedestrian. You must use extra caution, slow down, and be prepared to stop. Many states have specific laws requiring drivers to yield the right-of-way to pedestrians using a white cane or guide dog.

question: Why is a leaky exhaust system dangerous?
options: a:Carbon monoxide poisoning.,b:Pollution.,c:A loss of hearing.
note: A leaky exhaust can let carbon monoxide, a colorless and odorless gas, enter the passenger area. Breathing carbon monoxide can quickly cause headache, dizziness, unconsciousness, and even death. Any exhaust leak should be repaired immediately to prevent poisoning.

question: If involved in an accident, what should a driver do at the scene?
options: a:Stop near the scene, avoid standing in traffic lanes, and turn off ignitions of wrecked vehicles.,b:Leave the scene immediately if the damage is minor.,c:Stand in the middle of the road to direct traffic.,d:Drive to the nearest service station without stopping.
note: After a crash you must stop at or near the scene, stay out of moving traffic as much as possible, and turn off the ignitions of damaged vehicles to reduce fire risk. You must also check for injuries, call emergency services if needed, and provide any required help and information before leaving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where may you legally make a U-turn?
options: a:Where you can do so safely, legally, and without disrupting other traffic.,b:Near the top of a hill.,c:On a freeway.
note: You may make a U-turn only where it is both safe and legal. It must not interfere with other traffic, and you must obey any signs or markings that prohibit U-turns. U-turns are often illegal on freeways and near hills or curves where other drivers cannot see you in time.

question: What should be your first response when visibility is reduced?
options: a:Turn on your headlights,b:Reduce your speed,c:Turn on your windshield wipers,d:Pull over immediately
note: When visibility drops, you should immediately turn on your low‑beam headlights so others can see you. At the same time, adjust your speed to match what you can safely see ahead, and use wipers or defrosters as needed. Good lighting and an appropriate speed are both essential in low‑visibility conditions.

question: On slippery roads what should you do regarding following distance?
options: a:Drive as you would on dry roads.,b:Increase your following distance.,c:Use alternate routes.
note: On wet, icy, or otherwise slippery roads, your tires have less grip and it takes much longer to stop. Increase your following distance so you have more time and space to brake gently and avoid skids or rear‑end collisions.

question: Is it legal to park in the handicap parking access aisle next to a handicapped space?
options: a:False — parking in access aisles is prohibited.,b:True
note: You may not park in the striped access aisle next to a disabled parking space. That area is reserved so people using wheelchairs, walkers, or lifts have enough room to safely enter and exit their vehicles. Parking there blocks access and is illegal, even if you have a disabled placard or plate.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Minnesota law, by how much is the speed limit increased on a two-lane highway with a posted limit of 55 mph or higher when you are lawfully passing another vehicle?
options: a:5 mph,b:10 mph,c:15 mph,d:No increase is permitted while passing
note: In Minnesota, the speed limit on two-lane highways with a posted speed limit of 55 mph or higher is increased by 10 mph when the driver is lawfully passing another vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are convicted of driving a vehicle in Minnesota at a speed of 100 mph or faster, your driving privileges will be revoked for at least:
options: a:3 months,b:6 months,c:1 year,d:2 years
note: In Minnesota, if you are convicted of driving in excess of 100 miles per hour, your driver's license will be revoked for a period of at least six months.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In Minnesota, you must file a traffic crash report with the Department of Public Safety within 10 days if the crash results in injury, death, or total property damage of at least:
note: Minnesota law requires you to file a crash report within 10 days if the accident results in injury, death, or property damage of $1,000 or more.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a stopped school bus with its red lights flashing and stop arm extended on an undivided Minnesota road, you must stop your vehicle at least:
options: a:10 feet away,b:15 feet away,c:20 feet away,d:30 feet away
note: In Minnesota, drivers must stop at least 20 feet away from a school bus that has its red lights flashing and stop arm extended.
